target: Progress-bar 'lying' premise — simulated; premise correct, usual explanation wrong
reason: Variance alone does NOT produce the effect: with randomly varying item costs, naive linear extrapolation error decays smoothly as 1/sqrt(n) (14% at 5% done, 9% at 10%, 3% at 50%) — noisy early, no halfway cliff. NON-STATIONARITY does: if late work is heavier (finalize/index/flush), the estimator is BIASED and biased in ONE direction the whole way — -68% at 5%, -54% at 25%, -36% at halfway, -18% at 75%, -4% at 95%; negative = over-promises. So the bar does not lie until halfway then become honest; it lies in the same direction throughout, and halfway is where the lie drops below the annoyance threshold. Root cause: the estimator ASSUMES the middle looks like the beginning — it does not track the middle. CAVEAT: this is a simulation of estimator behaviour under an ASSUMED cost profile, NOT a measurement of real installers; it shows the mechanism is sufficient, not that real bars fail this way. Independent quantitative support for SCT's design goal ('data present != data trustworthy') without touching the unproven mechanism.

target: Item-bank method LOCKED: Option C, split inverted, gated on a 60-item pilot
reason: Hermes asked A/B/C + whether to tag difficulty. Answer required checking whether item COUNT is the binding constraint. IT IS NOT. MEASURED: 62 of 63 items in the current bank score exactly 1.00 in every arm; only LIT-12 varies. LOGIC 126/126, AUX 15/15, ARITH 12/12, TOOL 3/3 all at 100.0%. A ceiling item yields ZERO discordant pairs and McNemar is computed entirely from discordant pairs, so it contributes exactly zero information. Scaling 64->500 at the same difficulty yields ~492 items contributing nothing. SIMULATED (4000 reps/cell, paired McNemar n=500): item-difficulty SD from 0.0 to 1.4 moves power only 0.82->0.93 at p_base 0.95 and is flat or slightly NEGATIVE at lower p_base — because the paired design already differences item difficulty out. So difficulty tagging does NOT buy power (answer to Hermes q2: tag it for the secondary mixed model and reporting, but nobody may claim it as a power lever; raw item identity suffices for the pre-registered primary). THE REAL LEVER is intra-family correlation: templated clones share a skeleton, so DE = 1+(m-1)*ICC; at ICC=0.6 with 17 clones/family, 493 items behave like ~47 independent items — potentially LESS effective n than the existing 64-item bank, for 458 items of authoring. Fewer clones per family, more families: 8/family at ICC=0.2 gives n_eff~200. DECISION: Option C with the split INVERTED from Hermes's proposal — ~29 existing families x ~8 (not 12-17) + ~25-30 NEW families x ~8, total ~460-500 across ~55-60 families, difficulty target 70-85% baseline (NOT >=95%), family_id MANDATORY or ICC is uncomputable. GATED on a 60-item pilot (30 current-difficulty + 30 harder, 6 families x 10, 2 models spanning the band, 2 carriers, N=3, temp 0 = 720 trials vs 30,000 for the full run) which measures the two unknowns: real difficulty distribution and empirical family ICC. NOT CLAIMED: the ICC values are ASSUMED, demonstrating magnitude not measuring it; the empirical 0.063 from the current bank is uninterpretable at the ceiling (variance ~0.0002) and must not be cited as 'low'; the power figures assume independence and are therefore OPTIMISTIC under clustering.

IMPLEMENTED as ERRORs in itembank_lint.py v3: LEAK_FALLACY_NAME (fallacy named in prose, suppressed for >=3-option multiple-choice where naming IS the format), LEAK_TELL_PHRASE (evaluative giveaways), LEAK_VERDICT_TOKEN (keyed verdict appears in the stem BODY outside the answer-format instruction), LEAK_ASYMMETRIC_LENGTH (mean stem length differs >25% between answer classes — the tell no human reviewer catches and a generator is most likely to create). Six new controls all pass, including the multiple-choice negative (no false positive on the bank's existing format) and a regression showing all 24 real packs still exit 0. Measured baseline: 0 of 52 current stems name a fallacy in surface text, so the existing discipline is real and these checks defend it at 8x scale. WHAT I STILL REVIEW, deliberately small and falsifiable: the GENERATOR itself (systematic leaks live there; per-item review only finds sporadic ones) and a seed-drawn 10% random audit sample checked by truth table, with an acceptance-sampling rule — >=1 wrong key in the sample sends the whole batch back. TWO THINGS NO LINTER CAN CHECK, stated as generator requirements: (1) truth-table/Lean verification of every new key, with the formal_spec as SOURCE and surface text generated FROM it, never prose-first-then-annotated; (2) every trap paired to its non-trap sibling on the same skeleton, or a failure cannot be attributed to the trap versus the skeleton.

target: Pilot generator reviewed: 30/30 keys independently re-derived, GO with two conditions
reason: Wrote a separate propositional solver from scratch (own tokenizer, recursive-descent parser, truth-table evaluator) and re-derived EVERY key from formal_spec rather than the promised 10% sample. Result: 30/30 agreement, zero key mismatches, zero turnstile mismatches (the derived truth value also matches each spec's own vdash/nvdash glyph, so specs are internally consistent). Confirmed PILOT-F4-TRAP-DEM keyed FALSE and real De Morgan keyed TRUE — Hermes's self-caught bug and fix are both correct. Read the generator code: is_valid/is_equivalent/is_satisfiable enumerate all 2^n assignments, add() computes expected THEN renders spec and stem, so there is no path for a hardcoded answer — the spec-is-SOURCE requirement is genuinely met. Structural gates verified independently: mechanism split chain 10/trap 11/negdepth 9; 11/11 traps carry sibling_id AND every sibling exists in the bank; family_id on all 30 (ICC computable); scoring_method exact 30/30; answer-format instruction on 30/30; leakage gate 0 ERROR. CLEARED a confound I went looking for: bare-symbol vs domain-noun stems are balanced across mechanisms (chain 2/10, trap 2/11, negdepth 1/9), so a difficulty difference cannot be attributed to abstractness rather than logic. TWO CONDITIONS, non-blocking: (4a) key balance is 16/24 = 67% VALID on the VALID/INVALID subset — 95%CI [0.47,0.82], p=0.152 vs 50/50 so NOT statistically skewed at this N, but a model answering VALID unconditionally scores 67% without reading, and weak models default to a majority answer more readily than strong ones, which is precisely the difficulty signal being measured; rebalance to 12/12. (4b) report the combined 60-item balance including the 30 anchors, which I did not check this pass. MY OWN PROCESS FAILURE, recorded: my first run reported 38 disagreements including modus ponens keyed VALID vs my INVALID. MP failing is not a plausible generator bug, it is a tell that the CHECKER is broken — my tokenizer didn't handle Unicode operators so every formula parsed as atoms. I added self-checks (MP valid, affirming-consequent invalid, De Morgan holds, trap FALSE) BEFORE trusting any comparison. Had I shipped that output I'd have sent Hermes chasing 38 phantom bugs in a correct generator. A verifier that hasn't verified itself is not evidence — same class as the linter whose positive control couldn't distinguish the defect from normal operation.

target: REVIEW_pilot_generator.md §3 — leakage-gate row was RELAYED from Hermes under a heading claiming independent verification
reason: Found by audit. §3's heading read 'verified independently, not from the generator's own report', but the leakage figures (0 ERROR, 10 WARN) appeared ONLY in Hermes's paste-back — I never ran itembank_lint.py on the emitted pack. Every other row in that table traces to my own output; that one did not. The same misattribution went into the epistemic log entry. Relayed-as-self-verified class, aggravated because the heading explicitly promised otherwise. NOW ACTUALLY RUN: rendered the 30 items into an administered [NN] pack with extracted keys and ran itembank_lint.py --keys. FIRST RESULT: exit 1, 2 ERROR — LEAK_VERDICT_TOKEN on items 15 and 17, both keyed TRUE, both stems reading 'Is the following equivalence true?'. DIAGNOSED AS A FALSE POSITIVE IN MY OWN LINTER, not a bank defect: the interrogative 'Is X true?' is a question form, and the decisive evidence is internal to the bank — of the four 'Is ... true?' items, TWO are keyed TRUE (F4-DEMORGAN, F4-DIST) and TWO FALSE (F4-TRAP-DEM, F4-TRAP-DIST); a genuine leak would key all four alike. My check split on the last 'answer' occurrence so the interrogative use fell into the body region. FIXED: suppress an interrogative match (is/are/does ... <VERDICT> ?) while still firing on assertions. RE-VALIDATED: assertion positive control still fires, plus fallacy-name, tell-phrase and length-tell controls; all 24 real packs still exit 0. RE-RUN: exit 0, 0 ERROR, 10 WARN (all TOKEN_PLUS_PROSE) — the same numbers Hermes reported, but now derived by me, and the linter is one false positive better. NOTE THE COMPOUNDING: had I not been caught, a false positive in my own gate would have stayed hidden behind a number I trusted from someone else. Relaying a green result is worse than relaying a red one, because nobody re-checks a pass.

target: pilot_analysis.py — pre-registered analysis harness for the 60-item pilot, written BEFORE the data
reason: The pilot's three outputs (difficulty distribution, family ICC, per-mechanism difficulty) had NO harness; the existing carrier_color_analysis.py covers none of them (no ICC, no difficulty, no mechanism). Building the estimator after seeing the data is how a null becomes a finding, so the estimators, thresholds and go/no-go rule are now fixed in code. Computes: per-item difficulty with a target band 70-85%; family ICC via one-way ANOVA ICC(1) on per-item rates (chosen over a GLMM deliberately — no optimiser, cannot fail to converge, and the items-per-family cap table only needs ~0.1 resolution) feeding DE=1+(m-1)*ICC and a cap table; per-mechanism pass rates with Wilson CIs. Infra errors dropped as MISSING per the standing rule. VALIDATED with 6 controls, all passing: T1 ICC recovery from injected family SD 0.0/1.0/2.0 -> 0.055/0.359/0.615, strictly monotonic (the load-bearing control — an ICC estimator that cannot recover a known injected value is worthless and the whole design decision rests on it); T2 ceiling bank STOPs at 7% informative, off-ceiling bank PROCEEDs at 90%; T2b under-powered trial count warns; T3 injected-hardest mechanism recovered; T4 infra rows dropped not scored; T5 single family -> STOP rather than silent proceed.

target: My own ceiling-classification rule was biased — caught by my own failing control before it ran on data
reason: T2's off-ceiling case returned STOP on a healthy bank. Not a test bug: a measurement bias in my ceiling rule. An item with TRUE p=0.75 scores perfect on 3 trials 42% of the time (6 trials 18%, 12 trials 3%), so classifying 'at ceiling' from a small-N perfect score mislabels well-calibrated items as uninformative and would have STOPPED a good pilot — the opposite error from the one the pilot exists to prevent, and it would have been invisible because a STOP verdict looks like diligence. FIXED IN THE ESTIMATOR, NOT THE THRESHOLD: an item counts as at-ceiling only if it scored >=95% AND carried >=8 trials; perfect-but-under-powered items get their own reported field and are never silently folded into the ceiling count. Same shape as the LIT-12 lesson (a small number of repeats cannot resolve an item near its boundary), now enforced mechanically rather than remembered.

target: Pilot must report difficulty POOLED across models; per-model splits are descriptive only
reason: Computed from the specced design: 60 items x 2 models x 2 carriers x 3 reps = 720 trials = 12 trials/item POOLED, which clears the >=8 bar for a ceiling call. BUT per model it is only 2 carriers x 3 reps = 6 trials/item, and at 6 trials an item with true p=0.85 looks perfect 38% of the time (p=0.75: 18%). So per-model ceiling calls are under-powered. RULE: the go/no-go verdict consumes the POOLED difficulty; per-model splits are descriptive and must not be used to call an item 'ceiling for model X'. If a per-model ceiling call is actually needed for the capability-band question it requires N=6 reps (24 trials/item, 1,440 total) — worth deciding deliberately now rather than discovering at analysis time. The harness emits this warning itself from the observed trial count so it cannot be forgotten.

target: N=6 endorsed on verified grounds; the pooled-only caveat is retired by the design
reason: Carey called N=6 and Hermes proceeded without waiting — correct, the pilot is their lane and the go/no-go is a pre-built harness. Verified the call buys what it was meant to: per model, trials/item goes 6 -> 12, clearing MIN_TRIALS_FOR_CEILING=8, so PER-MODEL ceiling calls become valid. P(an item with true p=0.85 scoring perfect) drops 0.377 -> 0.142; p=0.75 drops 0.178 -> 0.032. Pooled is 4 conditions x 6 reps = 24 trials/item, 1,440 total. Ran the harness on a simulated N=6 pilot: median 24 trials/item, ZERO perfect-but-underpowered items (the entire concern at N=3), go/no-go clean, ICC estimated and cap emitted. So my v1 rule 'report difficulty POOLED, per-model is descriptive only' is now RETIRED — the design fixed the power problem rather than working around it.
supersedes: my 2026-07-26T09:22Z decision that per-model splits must be descriptive only

target: Hermes's plan to join pilot metadata to `tests` BY NAME — this is the 63-vs-64 defect, now blocked by a FATAL guard
reason: Hermes wrote: 'a companion pilot_items table holding the metadata + the pack, joined to tests by name at analysis time.' Name is not a key in this bank. Checked: the 30 GENERATED items are name-unique, but the 30 ANCHOR items come from the existing bank where 'AUX-APPROVAL-01 Benign Command Classification' maps to TWO distinct test_ids. If that item is among the anchors, a name join assigns one metadata row to two tests, and analyze() — which groups by item_id and takes metadata from the first row seen — MERGES their trials into one pseudo-item: inflated trials/item, wrong per-item pass rate, phantom item in the ICC. That is exactly the defect that cost 1,024 trials and was only caught in post-hoc analysis. HARDENED: pilot_analysis.py now raises SystemExit on either collision signature — one item_id carrying conflicting metadata, or one carrying a MULTIPLE of the modal trial count — and the message names the defect and the fix. Two new controls (T6): collision is fatal; clean data passes untouched. 8 controls now pass. The fix on Hermes's side is one line at emit time: key the CSV on test_id, the primary key, never the display name. A guard beats a reminder — the reminder is what failed last time.

target: Pilot runs 954-957: reported 1,536 trials implies 64 items, not the specced 60
reason: Arithmetic: 60 items x 2 models x 2 carriers x 6 reps = 1,440. The reported 1,536 / 24 trials-per-item = 64 items — four more than the design. Three candidates and the distinction matters: (a) the anchor set was drawn as 34 not 30, which changes the 30-current/30-harder balance the go/no-go reads and the difficulty comparison assumes; (b) the AUX-APPROVAL-01 twin came along — the bank has 64 distinct test_ids under 63 display NAMES, so selecting anchors by test_id legitimately includes the hidden twin while selecting by name would mean something duplicated; (c) four items were added deliberately and were not mentioned. Requested SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT test_id) on the pilot set. If 64 with a documented reason, only the design note needs updating; if 60, the run carries 96 trials that do not belong to the pilot.

target: 'Difficulty read pooled per carrier per model' is under-powered and would undo what N=6 bought
reason: 'Pooled' and 'per carrier per model' are opposite operations, and the GRANULARITY — not the run size — sets the power. Computed trials/item by reading: fully pooled 24 (powered), per model 12 (powered — this is exactly what N=6 bought), per carrier x model 6 (NOT powered, below the >=8 bar). At 6 trials an item with true p=0.85 reads perfect 38% of the time and p=0.75 reads perfect 18%, so a per-carrier-per-model ceiling call would label a large share of well-calibrated items uninformative and could STOP a healthy pilot — precisely the error N=6 was raised to eliminate. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION so this is not over-applied: the CARRIER CONTRAST is fine at 6 reps because it is a PAIRED within-item comparison and pairing is what makes it work; what is not fine is calling an item 'at ceiling' inside a single carrier x model cell. RULE: read DIFFICULTY and CEILING pooled or per-model; read the CARRIER EFFECT paired at any granularity. ENFORCED, not just stated: pilot_analysis.py v3 emits a stratification block computed from the OBSERVED data giving trials/item and a powered verdict for all four granularities, and the go/no-go text names which readings are valid. New control T7 verifies it against the real design shape. 9 controls pass. TEST-BUG NOTE: T7 failed on first run because my fixture emitted 6 rows per item TOTAL rather than 6 per cell — the fixture was wrong, not the code; I fixed the fixture and left the threshold untouched. Recorded because 'the test failed so I moved the threshold' is the exact move this project exists to catch.

target: Pilot STOP reproduced first-hand from pilot_results.csv (1,536 rows, sha256 feda070d12746f07)
reason: Ran the pre-registered harness unmodified on the committed CSV: exit 1, STOP. 64 items, 1,536 trials, 0 infra errors, overall pass 0.9915, 96.9% of items at ceiling, 2 informative, median item rate 1.00, min 0.75. All three mechanisms at 100% (chain 100.0, negdepth 100.0, trap 100.0, anchor 98.2). Hermes's reading of the verdict is correct and the pilot did its job: 1,536 trials spent to avoid 30,000 measuring nothing. RESOLVED my pre-run 64-vs-60 flag: the run IS 64 items, and the four extra are ALL TRAPS — the split is anchor 30 / chain 10 / trap 15 / negdepth 9, but the generator emitted 11 traps. So the mechanism comparison ran at 10/15/9, trap over-weighted 36%. target: 'ICC = 0.000, excellent, items independent, 500 real = 500 effective' — NOT supported; ICC is unmeasurable here
reason: ICC is a ratio of variances. In this data MS_between = 0.000866 < MS_within = 0.001747, so the raw ANOVA estimate is NEGATIVE and my harness clipped it to 0. Variance of per-item pass rates is 0.0017 because 62 of 64 items are exactly 1.0 — there is no variance to partition. Reading the clipped 0 as 'items are independent' converts a degenerate estimate into a design guarantee and would license n_eff = 500 for the full bank, the single most consequential number in the build plan. CORRECT STATEMENT: family ICC is NOT ESTIMABLE at this ceiling — unknown, not zero — and no items-per-family cap is justified by this data. FIXED IN MY OWN HARNESS: icc_anova now returns NaN when MS_between < MS_within instead of clipping to 0, and the go/no-go text says 'UNKNOWN, NOT ZERO: do not read it as items are independent and do not set a cap from it.' Control T8 added (constructed degenerate case, since a plain high-p ceiling does not reliably produce MS_between < MS_within); 10 controls pass. Re-ran the real pilot: ICC now reports nan, cap None.
supersedes: Hermes's pilot summary line 'Family ICC 0.000 — Excellent — items are independent, 500 real items = 500 effective'

target: I nearly reported a clustering artifact as a Carrier Color replication
reason: Digging past the STOP I found what looked like the pilot's positive result: gemma-4-e2b degrades under Lean (99.74% -> 96.88%) while nemotron-3-nano-omni is perfect in both carriers, Fisher p = 0.0032 on the 1,536 trial rows. That is the immunity-threshold pattern and I was one paragraph from reporting it as a replication. IT DOES NOT SURVIVE CLUSTERING. Fisher on trial rows treats each trial as independent; they are not — 24 trials per item, 6 reps each. The PRE-REGISTERED paired item-level test gives 3 lean-worse vs 1 baseline-worse discordant items, exact p = 0.625, NOT significant. A cluster-robust bootstrap resampling ITEMS (10k reps) gives mean per-item delta +0.029 with 95% CI [-0.003, +0.076], INCLUDING ZERO. So the trial-level p=0.003 is a clustering artifact and four discordant items cannot carry a claim. Honest statement: the direction is consistent with carrier sensitivity in the weaker model and immunity in the stronger, but the pilot has too little variance to establish it. Recorded because 'we found a significant carrier effect in the pilot' is exactly the sentence that would have escaped into the record — and it would have been MY sentence, in the same session where I corrected the same error class in others.

target: Next step: a 40-item difficulty PROBE at N=3, not another 500-item design and not a guess at a harder class
reason: Answering Hermes's (a)/(b) with (b), qualified. The pilot demonstrated that authoring difficulty a priori FAILS: three principled mechanisms, all null on both a 2B and a nano model. Repeating that with defeasible reasoning or quantifier scope is the same bet with a different noun. Instead: ~40 items, 4 candidate classes x 10, same 2 models, 2 carriers, N=3 = 960 trials. N=3 is correct here because the question is only 'does anything move off the ceiling' — a crude filter, not a measurement. Candidate classes ordered by evidence already in hand: (1) sound-argument / literary fallacy controls, the ONLY class that has ever bitten in this project (LIT-12 historically, and all 4 informative items in this pilot are anchors of that kind); (2) defeasible/default reasoning, non-monotonic so a memorised valid form does not transfer; (3) quantifier-scope ambiguity; (4) multi-hop with a DISTRACTOR premise — the chains that failed here had no irrelevant material. GATE: any class with >=30% of items off the ceiling graduates to a powered run; if none do, the finding is that this model class cannot be separated by formal-logic items at all, which is itself the answer to 'where is the immunity threshold' and a better paper than the one we set out to write. ALSO ESTABLISHED AND WORTH KEEPING: all 4 informative items are ANCHORS; the 34 purpose-built hard items contributed ZERO discordant pairs, so they are not merely as easy as the old bank, they are strictly less informative. NOT TO BE CONCLUDED: 'propositional logic is solved by modern models' — the items were authored to be hard, not representative, and 64 items on 2 models is not a survey.

target: Measured whether the house system prompt / double-prompting corrupts the science; answered the Frontier 'anti-scaffolding' advice
reason: MEASURED, not argued. The channel experiment already IS this experiment: manual channels B/C carry the vendor system prompt PLUS pasted battery instructions (doubly prompted); API channels A/A-prime carry fewer layers. Scores: A 189/192=98.44% [95.51,99.47]; A-prime 64/64=100% [94.34,100]; B 191/192=99.48% [97.11,99.91]; C 191/192=99.48%. Paired at item level (n=63): ONE discordant item, exact binomial p=1.000. CAUTION I nearly repeated: a per-item bootstrap returns a CI excluding zero, but 62 of 63 items are EXACTLY tied and the whole interval rides on one item — degenerate, same trap as the clustering artifact two turns earlier. HONEST VERDICT: no detectable difference between singly- and doubly-prompted channels, bounded ~+/-2 pts; NOT 'harmless' but 'not measurable at this ceiling' (items at 98-100% leave almost no resolving power). THE ARCHITECTURAL FINDING: the Google/Frontier advice is correct about out-of-band evaluation (which is already this project's architecture — itembank_lint.py, pilot_analysis.py, the Rust extract_verdict grader, the pre-registered go/no-go) but INVERTS when its linear anti-reflection state machine (INGEST->MAP->EXECUTE->VALIDATE->DELIVER, never loop back) is applied to the ANALYST rather than the SUBJECT. Evidence from this session's own log: 32 'correct' entries, 12 of them corrections of my own work caught by looping back, of which FOUR would have shipped as published findings — the carrier effect at Fisher p=0.0032 that was a clustering artifact (paired p=0.625); ICC=0.000 read as 'items independent' when it was not estimable (MS_between<MS_within); the 0%/100% isolation effect that was a grader bug; and 'validated unconditionally' from p=0.34. Under a strict one-pass pipeline all four ship. RULE ESTABLISHED: subject prompt must be pristine and identical across arms with self-checking FORBIDDEN (it corrupts the measurement); analyst prompt may be opinionated and self-checking is REQUIRED (it is the product). The house prompt has only ever been on the instrument. Subject purity is already enforced mechanically: packs byte-identical across channels, clean-room forced, key server-side, grading structural. THE ONE REAL RISK, already logged as DECISIONS §10.14 and still OPEN: the subject in manual channels is doubly prompted by a vendor prompt Carey does not control or see — a reason to prefer API arms for the primary measurement, not a reason to change his own operating instructions. ALSO: applying 'fail immediately and output the exact error trace' to the analyst would have CRASHED pilot_analysis.py on the pilot's ICC instead of reporting 'not estimable' — fail-fast on invariants, report-and-qualify on measurements.

target: My 'double-prompting is not measurably hurting anything, bounded ~+/-2 pts' — retracted on TWO counts, caught by Carey's pushback
reason: (a) THE BOUND WAS UNLICENSED. Computed power of the doubly-vs-singly comparison at the observed ceiling (manual 382/384=99.48%, API 253/256=98.83%): power 0.21 to detect a 1-pt drop, 0.55 for 2 pts, 0.80 only at 3 pts. So the test could not detect a 2-pt effect more than half the time and '+/-2 pts' was not supported; honest bound is +/-3 pts at best. 80% power for 2 pts needs ~600 items/arm, ~10x what ran. (b) THE LARGER ERROR: I answered a different question than the one asked. Carey's hypothesis is about PROCESS COST — how much capacity goes to reconciling instruction layers before reasoning starts. The channel experiment records a BINARY pass bit. Verified the instrument is structurally blind: format_ok and mappable are 1.0 in all four arms (zero variance) and tokens_completion/latency_ms exist for EXACTLY ONE arm (A-regraded, median 247 completion tokens). A model that reconciles conflicting prompts perfectly but burns 3x the tokens scores IDENTICALLY. Citing that data as evidence about reconciliation cost was a category error, not a small overreach. FAILURE CLASS: answering with the data I had rather than the data the question needed — and doing it in a memo whose whole subject was epistemic discipline.
supersedes: MEMO_prompt_architecture_double_modification.md v1 sections 0 and 1 verdict

target: SPEC_reconciliation_cost.md — 4-arm design measuring instruction-reconciliation cost in TOKENS, not accuracy
reason: Carey's question is a capacity-allocation claim: a system prompt is not only a constraint but a TASK performed before the asked task, consuming the same finite capacity. It predicts cost paid EVEN WHEN THE ANSWER IS RIGHT — invisible to accuracy. DESIGN: same 64 items, paired within item, temp 0, N=3, four arms — S0 no system prompt (single-layer baseline), S1 short neutral prompt (isolates HAVING a prompt from its CONTENT), S2 full house prompt aligned with the task (real-world condition), S3 layered prompt CONFLICTING on FORM with the task (reconciliation condition; must conflict on form, not on truth, or it becomes a refusal test). Primary outcome completion tokens; secondary latency at fixed temp (corroboration only, load-confounded); reasoning-trace length where exposed; ACCURACY DEMOTED TO A CONTROL. Pre-registered: H1 tokens(S1)>tokens(S0) = layering costs something; H2 tokens(S3)>tokens(S2)>tokens(S1) = the reconciliation tax, magnitude S3-S2; H3 (Carey's PERMISSION-GRANT reading, his own second hypothesis) accuracy(S2)>accuracy(S0) with tokens(S2)>tokens(S0) — the house prompt buys something at a token cost rather than being pure overhead, and this is the hypothesis that decides whether to keep it on subjects; H4 null across all arms = frontier models flatten instruction layers and the vendor system-prompt field is closer to theatre than control, also publishable. POWER: continuous outcome is ~10x cheaper than binary at a ceiling — 63 items/arm for d=0.5, 25 for d=0.8, versus ~600/arm for a 2-pt accuracy effect. 64 items x 4 arms x N=3 = 768 calls, SMALLER than the pilot that just STOPPED, and it escapes the ceiling because tokens vary even when every answer is correct. Same lesson as the pilot from the other direction: when the outcome is pinned, change the OUTCOME VARIABLE, not the sample size. Also answers the question I glossed: if frontier models ignore user system prompts, why does every vendor ship a field for one — either it does something measurable or it is theatre, and both are findings.

target: Prompt provenance must be DECLARED, HASHED and DETECTED — self-report alone is insufficient
reason: Carey's realization: subjects' system prompts must be honestly declared. Correct, and the repo already carries the scar. Read migrations first-hand: 046_quarantine_leaked_scaffold_runs.sql quarantined EVERY sealed scaffolded run because 'scaffolded runs with a non-empty scaffold_supplement had each test's formal_spec appended to the model's system prompt. The formal_spec IS the ground-truth answer ... those runs were handed an answer key.' answer_leak_contamination is one of only TWO quarantine reasons in the entire schema, and it is a PROMPT-LAYER contamination. CRUCIALLY, NOBODY LIED — the harness did it unconditionally in code. That is the empirical case for treating prompt provenance as a MEASURED variable, not a declared one. SCHEMA AUDIT (verified): test_runs.scaffold_supplement EXISTS (mig 029) and records the layer WE inject; load_mode EXISTS (mig 030); tests.fallacy_tag EXISTS. The subject's OWN system prompt is recorded NOWHERE, and `channel` appears in ZERO migrations (confirming Claude Code's flag). So the schema records the layer we add and is blind to the layers the subject already carries. PROPOSED: add subject_prompt_declared, subject_prompt_sha256, subject_prompt_source (enum authored_by_us|operator_declared|vendor_unknown|undeclared), and the missing channel column — with vendor_unknown and undeclared as FIRST-CLASS values, because a run honestly marked vendor_unknown is usable with a caveat while a run marked 'none' that had a hidden layer is corrupt. Plus quarantine reason prompt_provenance_unknown. WHY SELF-REPORT CANNOT SUFFICE, four reasons none requiring dishonesty: vendor prompts are unpublished and change silently (the open §10.14 confound); users do not know their own stack (earlier this session Carey's own bot silently auto-loaded a different model than selected); the harness is itself a layer and is the one that already contaminated us; and a declaration is a claim about hidden state, which by this project's own rule gets verified rather than accepted — we reject 'status: PASS' from a file, so we cannot accept 'system_prompt: none' from a form. DETECTION (my lane): (1) token/latency signature — per SPEC_reconciliation_cost.md an extra instruction layer costs completion tokens even when accuracy is unchanged, so a run declared single-layer whose token distribution matches the layered arms is evidence of an UNDECLARED layer; this makes the reconciliation-cost experiment a CALIBRATION OF THE DETECTOR, a second reason to run it. (2) behavioural canary items whose response is known to differ under a system prompt, administered with every run.

target: Standing rule: capability-independent failure is a DEFECT signal, not a difficulty measurement
reason: Carey named the harder problem: 'that's also me taking a test about to fail it because I disagree with the logical choices and the question itself. I know damn well the answer if the test maker hadn't fucked up the logic.' THIS PROJECT HAS A RECORDED INSTANCE: LOGIC-03N read 'revokes a key PRECISELY WHEN reported compromised' — a biconditional marker — but was keyed as one-directional; sibling LOGIC-01N used 'exactly when' and WAS keyed as a biconditional. Same marker, opposite keys. Replit answered correctly for the item AS WORDED and was SCORED AS A MISS until adjudicated (verified at the time by truth table under both readings, by both bots independently). THE DISCRIMINATING SIGNATURE, and it is computable: a genuinely hard item shows the stronger model doing better than the weaker; a DEFECTIVE item shows both failing at indistinguishable rates, because capability does not help you answer a question whose key is wrong. CHECKED ON THE PILOT: all four varying items show the CAPABILITY signature (gemma-4-e2b 0.50/0.58/0.92/0.92 vs nemotron 1.00 on each) — no defect signature present. BUT only 4 of 64 items varied at all, so that test is near-powerless and this is a standing check to install, NOT evidence of cleanliness. STANDING RULE: any item where models of clearly different capability fail at statistically indistinguishable rates is flagged for KEY REVIEW before it counts as difficulty. That automates what Replit did by hand, and per the log the LOGIC-01N/03N defect is the only defect class in this project ever caught by a SUBJECT rather than an author. THE PRINCIPLE: an instrument that cannot distinguish 'the subject is wrong' from 'the question is wrong' will publish the second as the first, and the more capable the subject the likelier it is the instrument at fault. The subject's disagreement is DATA, not noise.

reason: I probed for files that hold system prompts (~/.hermes/config.yaml, ~/.ollama, LM Studio app-support dir, ~/.claude.json, ~/.continue/config.json, ~/.codex, ~/.config/io.datasette.llm) and every one returned 'absent'. target: Surface taxonomy: 4 provenance tiers, tier COMPUTED not declared, and never ask the user for their system prompt
reason: Verified from src/: every native provider calibration-scope supports is an API provider (gemini 12 refs, nous 11, openrouter 10, openai 10, lmstudio 2); load_mode is exactly clean-room|scaffolded. That single fact reorganizes the problem. TIERS: P0 cloud API — we author the prompt byte-for-byte, provenance TOTAL; P1 local runner with an HTTP API (LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) — provenance TOTAL *if* we send an explicit system message, UNKNOWN if we omit the field; P2 desktop chat app (Claude Desktop, ChatGPT app, Hermes Desktop) — vendor prompt plus possibly user custom instructions, unpublished and version-drifting, provenance IMPOSSIBLE; P3 web chat UI — same plus session state and A/B assignment, IMPOSSIBLE and unstable. THE CRITICAL LINE IS P1/P2 AND IT IS NOT LOCAL-VS-CLOUD, it is 'does the harness author the prompt' — the same weights are P1 through LM Studio's API and P2 through its chat window. THE P1 TRAP: LM Studio and Ollama let a user save a system-prompt preset in the UI; if our request omits the system field that preset applies silently and we are in P2 believing we are in P1. RULE: always send an explicit system message, including an explicitly empty one, never omit the field. THE REFRAME THAT DISSOLVES CAREY'S PROBLEM: OPERATOR (the assistant that helps a human install and interpret — ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Hermes, a printed sheet) is out-of-band and NEVER MEASURED, so its prompt is irrelevant; SUBJECT is whatever the harness sends items to over an API, so provenance is total by construction. Therefore 'what is your system prompt?' is a question about the operator and must NOT be asked — asking invites a confident wrong answer (no user tracks 'before/after this morning' edits), implies the answer affects validity, and a recorded-but-false declaration is MORE corrupting than an honest unknown because it looks like provenance. INSTEAD: ask 'which app will the model answer in?' — a question about a SURFACE, which users can answer correctly and which determines the tier deterministically. Tag every run with provenance_tier computed by the harness from the code path taken; tier gates the claim in code (P2/P3 admissible for within-subject paired comparisons, excluded from cross-model leaderboards by the same mechanism that already excludes quarantined runs); for P1 record system_prompt_sha256 of what WE SENT — a fact about our own request, not a claim about hidden state. This removes the human from the trust path entirely.

target: ICD 203 adopted as the TERMINATING verification layer (Analytic Ombuds pattern), NOT as a compliance checklist
reason: Carey asked why ICD 203 wouldn't be involved as another verification layer, and separately worried about 'incepting ourselves to death'. ICD 203 answers both because it already solved the regress — by TERMINATING it structurally. Primary source (dni.gov ICD-203 + ODNI): the ODNI Analytic Ombuds 'reports directly to the Deputy Director for Mission Integration and operates independently of the analytic production chain'. That is the mechanism: you do not stop infinite self-review by reviewing harder, you put ONE checker OUTSIDE the production chain and declare the chain closed. Depth 2, bounded. Our equivalent already exists and I had not recognised it as one — the external auditor that keeps catching my claims IS the Ombuds, outside my chain by construction because it reads output not intent. DESIGN RULE: when a new 'who checks that?' feeling arrives, the answer is never another layer INSIDE the chain, it is route it to the entity outside; if none exists for that claim class, build ONE, not a hierarchy. COVERAGE MAPPED against the nine tradecraft standards: STRONG on 1 (source quality — sha256/run ids/committed CSV hashes), 3 (separating info from assumption — 'what is NOT established', relayed-vs-verified labels), 6 (clear argumentation — truth tables, pre-registration), 7 (explain change in judgments — the supersedes field IS this standard); MEASURED on 8 (40 corrections logged, the trail is the evidence); PARTIAL on 2, 5, 9; WEAK on 4 (analysis of alternatives) — THE REAL HOLE: every surprise this session (0%/100% isolation, carrier p=0.003, ICC=0.000) was correctly diagnosed only AFTER it looked like a finding, whereas standard 4 writes the rival explanation down FIRST. EXPLICITLY REJECTED: 'ICD 203 compliant' as a claim. The directive is a rating scale and a cited critique notes it 'suggests to its readers that one must meet all of the standards, but fails to provide measures of success' — a framework with nine boxes invites scoring nine boxes, which is exactly the pretty badge Carey's standard forbids. Adopt as GATES on specific claim types; no document may ever say 'ICD 203 compliant'.

target: My 'never ask the user for their system prompt' was too absolute — Carey is right
reason: I wrote that asking is 'worse than useless'. Overstated. target: Prior-art check: we are NOT first, and the mechanism already exists in Carey's own dns-tool-intel
reason: Carey asked for confirmation from NASA or others rather than reinventing. THE LO-FI FINDING FIRST: dns-tool-intel already has go-server/internal/citation/registry.yaml with 62 registered citations, including odni:icd-203 as a first-class entry (type: directive, publisher: ODNI, status: active, functional_area: intelligence) alongside iso:25012 (Data Quality Model), NIST SP 800-53, and a quality-gate functional area. calibration-scope has NO citation registry — no src/citation/, no registry.yaml, no CITATIONS.md; it mentions ICD 203 four times in prose with nothing enforcing it. Meanwhile GRADE (clinical evidence grading) appears 145 times in calibration-scope, unregistered. So the lo-fi move is to PORT registry.yaml, not build a subsystem. CONVERGENT PRIOR ART, three independent fields: (1) NASA-STD-7009A (Models & Simulation credibility) requires reporting best estimate, uncertainty statement, credibility assessment, explicit caveats including use in violation of assumptions, and RISKS OF ACCEPTING THE RESULTS — a five-field contract of which we already emit four informally; item 5 we never write down. (2) NASA's CoLD scale (7 levels, Green et al. 2021, Nature) independently reinvented both our contamination check ('ruling out contamination from earth based sources' = our answer_leak_contamination quarantine) AND ICD 203 standard 4 ('a biological interpretation... considered as a last resort after all other explanations have been exhausted') without reference to ICD 203. (3) The Biosignatures Standards of Evidence Workshop concluded assessment 'may need to depend on an external body' — the ODNI Analytic Ombuds structure reached from scratch by a third field. Three fields, one answer: the assessor must be outside the producer.

target: NASA-STD-7009A states the anti-badge rule as an engineering standard — adopt its wording, not a compliance score
reason: Verbatim from NASA-STD-7009A: 'This NASA Technical Standard itself levies no requirements with respect to what levels to achieve (the sufficiency threshold levels), merely that the levels be determined and reported.' NASA explicitly REFUSES to set a passing threshold — you must determine and report the level, you cannot score it. That is Carey's badge-chasing prohibition expressed as an engineering standard by a space agency, and it is stronger evidence for the rule than anything I wrote; it also retro-justifies the standing decision that no document in this project says 'ICD 203 compliant'. THREE ADOPTIONS, all small: (a) port registry.yaml from dns-tool-intel and register odni:icd-203, nasa:std-7009a, grade, iso:25012 — existing pattern, existing format, zero invention, Claude Code or Hermes lane; (b) adopt NASA-7009A's five-field report contract as the shape of every result note, the missing field being RISKS OF ACCEPTING THE RESULT which is precisely what a tool user needs; (c) steal CoLD's ladder structure for the difficulty probe — 7 levels where level 1 is 'signal observed' and upper levels require INDEPENDENT instruments, which makes 'we saw something but ruled out nothing' a reportable state instead of a null. CAVEAT ON MY OWN SOURCING: these were read from indexed search excerpts, NOT the primary PDFs. NASA-STD-7009A and the CoLD paper must be fetched and read before anything is built on them. And no claim that adopting any of this improves ACCURACY — it improves REPORTABILITY, which is a different and more defensible thing, as the NASA quote itself says.

target: DNS Tool's ICD-203 usage audited against the PRIMARY SOURCE (Carey's own Zotero copy) — usage is LEGITIMATE
reason: Carey granted ~/Zotero and asked me to check whether he is misusing ICD-203 ('make sure this kid didn't just get some crazy thought in his head about spy movies'). Found and read the directive itself at ~/Zotero/storage/W3KCQHUF/ICD-203.pdf (8pp, 19,350 chars, the AMENDED version) — no secondary sources used. VERDICT: not misuse, and the directive authorizes the usage in its own POLICY section: 'IC Analytic Standards shall be applied in each analytic product in a manner appropriate to its purpose, the type and scope of its underlying source information, its production timeline, and its customers. IC elements may create supplemental analytic standards that are tailored to their particular mission.' APPLICABILITY scopes WHOM THE DIRECTIVE BINDS (IC elements; excludes purely law-enforcement information) — it makes no exclusivity claim and does not prohibit external adoption. VOCABULARY CHECK, the one hard 'must' in the directive ('For expressions of likelihood or probability, an analytic product must use one of the following sets of terms', seven bands 01-05/05-20/20-45/45-55/55-80/80-95/95-99%, two interchangeable rows, 'strongly encouraged not to mix terms from different rows'): audited every user-facing Go string literal and HTML template across the repo excluding vendored gomod/ and the zenodo-repro/ archive — row-1 terms only (unlikely, likely), ZERO row-2 terms, no mixing, no disclaimer needed. The three 'probable' hits in posture.go are Go identifiers (probableNoMail, detectProbableNoMail), confirmed by extracting quoted strings only — false positive dismissed. posture.go even carries the comment 'judgment and analytic confidence are separate declared axes', which is standard 2's own distinction implemented deliberately. BADGE CHECK: grepped every template and doc for ICD 203 within 60 chars of compliant/compliance/certified/accredited — ZERO hits; live language is 'applies', 'aligned with', 'paralleling', 'per ICD 203'. Adoption described, conformity never claimed. CITATIONS.md archives both the amended and original 2015 PDFs.

target: dns-tool-intel go-server/templates/confidence.html — factually misdescribes ICD-203 AND commits the D.2.b conflation it prohibits
reason: The page states: 'The five-tier grading scale maps the continuous score to actionable categories, paralleling how ICD 203 maps analytic confidence to five levels (almost no confidence through high confidence).' THREE FACTUAL ERRORS, all verified against the primary PDF: (1) ICD-203 defines NO confidence levels — the phrase 'confidence level' appears exactly TWICE in the whole directive, both in the SAME sentence, and only as an example '(e.g., "high confidence")'; there is no enumerated confidence scale anywhere in it. (2) 'almost no confidence' appears ZERO times; the real term is 'almost no chance' and it belongs to the LIKELIHOOD table, not to confidence. (3) The table has SEVEN bands, not five. AND THE SENTENCE COMMITS THE ERROR THE DIRECTIVE EXPLICITLY PROHIBITS — D.2.b: 'products that express an analyst's confidence in an assessment or judgment using a "confidence level" (e.g., "high confidence") must not combine a confidence level and a degree of likelihood, which refers to an event or development, in the same sentence.' The copy borrows a LIKELIHOOD term to name CONFIDENCE tiers, which is exactly the conflation D.2.b exists to prevent, on a page whose subject is rigor. SEVERITY: same class as the carrier-immunity README overclaim — a documentation surface asserting what the underlying work does not support. IT IS A COPY DEFECT, NOT AN ENGINE DEFECT: the code keeps the two axes separate (posture.go comment above); only the explanatory page conflates them. FIX (Claude Code lane, one sentence): 'The five-tier grading scale maps the continuous score to actionable categories. This is DNS Tool's own scale — ICD 203 does not define confidence tiers; it mandates a seven-band LIKELIHOOD vocabulary and requires that likelihood and confidence never be combined in one statement. We keep them as separate declared axes.' NOT AUDITED: whether the confidence ENGINE is statistically sound (different audit, untouched by this finding); the ~60 archived reference PDFs; scispace_corpus/ markdown (row-1 hits there are quoted literature, not tool output); ICD 206, which ICD-203 references for source summary statements and which CITATIONS.md may not archive.

target: dns-tool-intel go-server/internal/analyzer/remediation.go — a genuine ICD-203 row mix my failed scan had missed
reason: The real 753-file scan found what the failed one could not. remediation.go, verbatim: label: "Probable No-Mail Domain — Needs Formal Declaration". 'Probable' is a ROW-2 likelihood term, while every other user-facing analytic judgment in the tool uses ROW 1 — posture.go: "Unlikely — SPF and DMARC quarantine policy enforced", "Likely — SPF alone cannot prevent spoofing". So the product DOES mix rows, and ICD-203 is explicit: 'Analysts are strongly encouraged not to mix terms from different rows. target: analysis/probe_items.json (commit e404451) — BLOCKING length leak on the sound-arg CONTROL class, found before administration
reason: Audited the 40-item difficulty probe BEFORE it runs (no probe_results.csv exists anywhere in the repo, so this was free). itembank_lint.py fired 1 ERROR LEAK_ASYMMETRIC_LENGTH (bank-wide mean stem length differs 119% across answer classes). Checked whether that was a pooling artifact across the four differently-shaped question formats: PARTLY YES, and the residue is worse than the headline. Within-class spread is defeasible 1%, distractor 0%, quant-scope 18% — all with OVERLAPPING ranges, no tell. But sound-arg is 43% and PERFECTLY SEPARABLE: NONE (the control) spans 341-361 chars (n=3) while every fallacy item spans 235-274 (n=7). ZERO OVERLAP, 67-char gap. The rule 'answer NONE if the stem exceeds 300 characters' scores 10/10 on that class without reading a single argument. The tell is in the ARGUMENT BODY not the shared boilerplate (the 132-char instruction tail is identical class-wide): NONE bodies are 229/209/214 chars, fallacy bodies 103-142 — the sound arguments were written with more supporting detail, realistic prose but diagnostic. WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A GENERIC LEAK, two compounding reasons: (a) it sits on the CONTROL, the one item type whose job is to prove a model is not merely pattern-matching 'a fallacy is expected here' — a guessable control cannot discriminate, which is the entire reason the class exists; (b) it MANUFACTURES A FALSE CEILING — the probe's purpose is to find items OFF the ceiling, so a length-guessable class returns high scores for the wrong reason, reads as 'still at ceiling', and makes the probe report STOP when the true answer was 'this class was never tested'. That STOP would look identical to a real one. FIX (Hermes lane, ~20 min): add 3-4 fallacy items with LONG bodies (200-240 chars) so the ranges overlap — non-destructive, keeps every existing item, and a long detailed still-fallacious argument is a harder and more realistic item than a short one. Rejected the alternative of trimming NONE bodies: shortening a sound argument removes the detail that makes it sound. GATE: re-run itembank_lint.py and require 0 ERROR before administering. ALSO FLAGGED: sound-arg has 5 answer classes over 10 items with CIRCULAR n=1 — a single item supports no per-mechanism rate; drop it or raise to 3. NOT AUDITED: analysis/generate_probe_items.py (12.6KB, whether it reproduces the JSON) and migrations/050_difficulty_probe.sql (whether the DB copy matches); if those disagree my audit applies to the JSON only. AND THE FINDING IS STRUCTURAL NOT BEHAVIOURAL — I showed a length rule COULD score 10/10, not that any model DOES use it; that is the right basis for a pre-administration gate but is not a measured model behaviour. FIX TO MY OWN TOOL: LEAK_ASYMMETRIC_LENGTH should report per-class, since its bank-wide figure is the right coarse alarm and the wrong final number.

target: My length-leak FALSE-CEILING prediction on the probe's sound-arg NONE items — FALSIFIED by the actual run
reason: One turn earlier I flagged sound-arg NONE as a blocking length leak (stems perfectly separable, 341-361 vs 235-274 chars, zero overlap, so 'answer NONE if >300 chars' scores 10/10 without reading) and predicted a FALSE CEILING: high scores for the wrong reason producing a STOP indistinguishable from a real one. MEASURED from probe_results.csv (480 rows, runs 958-961, commit 285ea41): NONE = 0.139 pass over 36 trials; every fallacy item = 1.000 over 84 trials; item-level Mann-Whitney n=3 vs 7 p=0.005. The models did NOT exploit the tell — they failed the long items catastrophically. The length rule was AVAILABLE and UNUSED. The gate was still correct in principle (close a leak because it is reachable, not because someone was caught using it) but the specific harm I predicted did not occur and the class is not compromised. Recording as a falsified prediction, not a save. Also, my own LEAK_ASYMMETRIC_LENGTH bank-wide figure of 119% was substantially a pooling artifact across four differently-shaped question formats; within-class spreads were defeasible 1%, distractor 0%, quant-scope 18%, sound-arg 43%. Fix to my own tool: report per-class.

target: Probe results verified and reinterpreted — the sound-arg finding is a NONE-response bias across the whole control class
reason: All four of Hermes's off-ceiling rates reproduce exactly from the CSV: quant-scope 6/10=60%, defeasible 5/10=50%, sound-arg 3/10=30%, distractor 2/10=20%. THE REAL SOUND-ARG FINDING: all 3 off-ceiling items are the NONE controls and all 7 fallacy items are perfect. On fallacy items models were right 100% (they named a fallacy every time); on NONE items right 14% (they named a fallacy almost every time). The models essentially NEVER volunteer NONE. Hermes called items 127/128 'the new LIT-12-class items' — CONFIRMED and broader: it is the entire control class, same over-calling signature as LIT-12 in the channel experiment. APPLIED THE STANDING CAPABILITY-INDEPENDENCE RULE: item 126 is capability-dependent (gemma 0.83 vs nemotron 0.00) = real difficulty; items 127 and 128 are BOTH exactly 0.00 on both models = defect signature, key review required before counting as difficulty. ADJUDICATED ON THE MERITS AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME CASE. 127 ('two independent reviewers flagged the same 4 of 30 logs... their agreement suggests the 4 share a detectable property'): key NONE is CORRECT — inter-rater agreement as evidence of a detectable signal is standard methodology, conclusion is hedged, and the only candidate HASTYGEN does not apply because the conclusion concerns detectability not a population. Both models are simply wrong; this is the single most valuable item in the probe. 128 ('after we enabled connection pooling, latency fell 180ms->40ms holding hardware and query mix constant, pooling PLAUSIBLY reduced latency'): AMBIGUOUS — NONE is defensible (controlled before/after, hedged) but FALSECAUSE is also defensible (no control group, single intervention, post-hoc ordering = textbook post hoc ergo propter hoc); the word 'plausibly' carries the entire key and 'exactly one word' forces a binary onto a graded judgment. That is the LOGIC-03N pattern again. Reword 128, keep 127.

target: Possible instrument defect across the whole sound-arg class: the stem presupposes a fallacy exists
reason: The stem reads 'Which single rhetorical fallacy best describes it? Answer with exactly one word: FALSECAUSE, HASTYGEN, CIRCULAR, ADPOPULUM, or NONE.' That question PRESUPPOSES a fallacy. NONE is offered but the framing argues against choosing it. So the 14% NONE rate has two competing explanations that this data CANNOT distinguish: H_bias (the leading stem induces a fallacy-expectation — an artifact of OUR wording) versus H_deficit (the models genuinely cannot recognise a sound argument — a real capability finding). DISCRIMINATING TEST, 36 calls: re-administer the 3 NONE items under a neutral framing ('Does this argument commit a rhetorical fallacy? If so, name it; if not, answer NONE.') alongside the current wording — 2 models x 3 reps x 2 framings. If the neutral framing substantially raises the NONE rate, the 14% was our stem, not their reasoning. THIS MUST RUN BEFORE the powered design treats sound-arg as a difficulty source, because the entire class's off-ceiling status rests on it. UNTIL IT RUNS, 'models cannot recognise sound arguments' is a HYPOTHESIS, not a finding, and must not enter any public copy.

target: Powered-run bank size: ~120-130 items across the 3 graduating classes, NOT 8-12 per family
reason: Only OFF-CEILING items can produce discordant pairs, so they are the only ones supplying McNemar power. Measured off-ceiling yield: quant-scope 6/10 (failures at 0.25/0.25/0.50/0.50/0.50/0.92), defeasible 5/10 (0.25/0.25/0.50/0.50/0.75), sound-arg 3/10 (0.00/0.00/0.42), distractor 2/10 (does not graduate). Class pass rates with Wilson 95%: quant-scope 0.692 [0.604,0.767], defeasible 0.725 [0.639,0.797], sound-arg 0.742 [0.657,0.812], distractor 0.900 [0.833,0.942]. Earlier this session: McNemar needs ~25 items at d=0.8 and ~63 at d=0.5. At the measured ~50% off-ceiling yield, a bank of ~120-130 items across the three graduating classes yields ~60 informative ones. Hermes's option (b) at 8-12 per family gives roughly 24-36 items total and perhaps 15 informative — under-powered for anything but the largest effect. QUANT-SCOPE SHOULD GET THE MOST ITEMS: highest off-ceiling yield AND its failures sit at 0.25-0.50, mid-range, the most informative region far from both ceiling and floor. RECOMMENDED SEQUENCE, answering Hermes's (a)/(b)/(c): neither (a) nor (b) as posed — (1) run the 36-call framing test first, (2) reword 128 and keep 127, (3) then build the expanded bank at ~120-130 items weighted toward quant-scope, linted before administration. CAVEATS: the CSV keys on DB integer ids 126-165, not names — I verified contiguous block-ordering matching the JSON's class order so the id-to-item mapping is sound, but it is an INFERENCE FROM ORDERING and a test_id/name column would remove the assumption; and quant-scope/defeasible off-ceiling items have NOT been individually adjudicated for key correctness, which at 0.25-0.50 is exactly where a keying defect would hide.

target: Powered-run bank size (~120-130 items / ~60 informative) — derived from a power figure TRANSPLANTED across designs
reason: Audit finding confirmed with a margin. I cited 'McNemar needs ~25 items at d=0.8, ~63 at d=0.5 (computed earlier this session)' and built the recommendation on it. Those numbers are NOT a McNemar requirement: they came from n_per_arm(d)=2*((za+zb)/d)**2, a TWO-SAMPLE T-TEST sizing for a CONTINUOUS completion-token outcome, PER ARM, computed for the separate reconciliation-cost design. I transplanted a continuous-outcome Cohen's d into a PAIRED-BINARY design where the effect is a difference in pass proportion and power depends on discordant-pair supply. It also contradicted my own earlier McNemar work this session, which used ~500 items to reach power 0.82-0.93 for carrier deltas of 0.05-0.10 — I had the right number in front of me and used the wrong one. PROPER SIMULATION, driven by the probe's measured off-ceiling rates (n=14 items: 0.00,0.00,0.25,0.25,0.25,0.25,0.42,0.50,0.50,0.50,0.50,0.50,0.75,0.92; mean p0=0.40), item-level McNemar with one scoring per item per carrier: 25 informative items -> power 0.03/0.06/0.22 at d=0.05/0.10/0.20; 60 -> 0.06/0.16/0.59; 100 -> 0.09/0.28/0.84; 200 -> 0.16/0.55/0.99; 400 -> 0.30/0.85/1.00. So my '~60 informative items' gives power 0.16 at d=0.10, NOT 0.80. WHAT RESCUES IT: repeated scoring per cell (majority-vote within carrier) suppresses measurement noise so discordance reflects true per-item differences — at d=0.10, 150 informative items go 0.42 (1 rep) -> 0.67 (3) -> 0.90 (6); at d=0.20, 60 items go 0.59 -> 0.82 -> 0.97. REPS ARE CHEAPER THAN AUTHORING: 6 reps at 150 items beats 1 rep at 400. REVISED, at the measured 14/30 = 47% off-ceiling yield: ~128 authored items at 3 reps buys a LARGE-effect test ONLY (d>=0.20, power 0.82); locating the immunity threshold — §10.9's actual question, needing ~10-point resolution — requires ~320 authored items at 6 reps (power 0.90); d=0.05 is out of reach at any feasible bank size and should be declared out of scope in the design rather than discovered later. My ~120-130 floor was not wrong as a number, it was wrong about what it buys. NEW FAILURE CLASS FOR ME: transplanting a power number across designs — a UNIT error, distinct from my recurring verify-a-subset-certify-the-set. It drove the headline recommendation in two artifacts and a chat bottom line. STANDING RULE ADDED: a power figure may only be cited with its test, its outcome type and its units attached; if reused, re-derive it in the new design rather than quoting it. The tell I should have caught: 'items per arm' — a between-groups quantity — appearing in a within-item paired design, which has no arms.

target: framing_test_pack.json primary_test and power — I PRE-REGISTERED the trial-level independence error I had already retracted this session
reason: Second audit finding on this design and the more serious one. The pack declared primary_test 'McNemar on NONE items, framing A vs B, paired within item+model+rep' and power 'McNemar on 90 NONE pairs: 0.97 ... 1.00 at 0.139->0.50'. That treats 15 repetitions of the same 3 items as 90 independent observations. EARLIER THIS SAME SESSION I retracted exactly this error: a carrier effect at trial-level Fisher p=0.0032 that collapsed to p=0.625 under an item-level paired test and a cluster bootstrap, because repeated measurements of one item are not independent. I then wrote the retracted form into a PRE-REGISTRATION. Worse, my simulator drew n independent Bernoulli pairs so it could not represent the correlation at all, and I stated the caveat ('reps are correlated within item') in the same cell whose model ignored it — a caveat is not a control. REAL STRUCTURE: 3 NONE items x 2 models = 6 CLUSTERS with 15 correlated reps inside each cell. CLUSTER-AWARE POWER (unit = (item,model) cell, majority vote within cell, n_units=6), at a 0.139->0.50 rise: reps=3 -> 0.01, reps=6 -> 0.03, reps=15 -> 0.03, reps=30 -> 0.05. MY PRE-REGISTERED FIGURE WAS 1.00; THE TRUE VALUE IS 0.03. The 420-call run as designed would have returned a null essentially regardless of the truth, and I would have reported that null as 'H_deficit survives' — a wrong conclusion with a pre-registration behind it. REPS CANNOT FIX IT, the cluster count caps power: 3 NONE items (6 units) 0.03, 6 items (12 units) 0.72, 10 items (20 units) 0.98, 15 items 1.00 — adding items buys everything, adding reps almost nothing, which is the opposite of what I told Hermes ('reps are the only lever'). ONE ALTERNATIVE IS LEGITIMATE AT n=6: treating each cell's pass RATE as continuous and running a paired t-test on 6 cells gives power 0.91 at a 0.40 rise and 0.99 at 0.50 with reps=15, and I CHECKED ITS CALIBRATION — null control false-positive rate 0.043-0.046 at alpha=0.05, correctly sized; Wilcoxon also works (power 0.90, FP 0.005, min attainable two-sided p=0.031). BUT the item-level generalization is still n=3 and leave-one-out sensitivity shows 23% of 'significant' results FLIP when any single item is dropped, so a positive licenses only 'these 3 arguments behave differently under neutral framing', not 'models can recognise sound arguments'. REVISED DESIGN: NONE items are simply sound arguments with no fallacy to construct — the easiest item type to write — so author 7 more, giving 10 NONE + 10 mechanism-balanced fallacy controls x 2 models x 6 reps = 480 calls, McNemar power 0.98 with honest cluster structure and a 20-item generalization base; primary test McNemar at the (item,model) CELL level with reps as noise reduction WITHIN a cell rather than units; secondary the calibrated continuous test; report leave-one-item-out sensitivity with any positive; stopping rule unchanged. The 6-cell continuous test at 15 reps (168 calls) may run today as a PILOT SIGNAL ONLY, explicitly not the class verdict; the McNemar form must not run at 3 items under any rep count. PROCESS FAILURE: two power errors in consecutive turns of DIFFERENT classes — the first a unit error (continuous-outcome Cohen's d transplanted into a paired-binary design), this one an independence error (clustered observations counted as independent). What they share: I simulated a design simpler than the one I was proposing, and the simulator's simplicity hid the flaw. STANDING RULE ADDED: a power simulation must instantiate the actual clustering of the design — items, models and reps as separate levels; if the simulator draws a flat vector of n independent units, the design had better have n independent units. And the specific tell: I stated the correlation caveat in prose while my code ignored it. When those disagree, the code is wrong and the prose is decoration.
supersedes: framing_test_pack.json v1 primary_test and power; NEXT_STEPS_calibration_scope.md item 1 reps table

target: '6-cell continuous test at 15 reps (168 calls)' — budget and power came from DIFFERENT rows; propagated to 3 artifacts, the log and chat prose
reason: Third audit finding on this design, confirmed. I wrote '15 reps (168 calls)' and attached the 15-rep power figures (0.91 @0.40 / 0.99 @0.50) to it. 168 is the SIX-rep budget: the pack is 14 prompts = (3 NONE + 4 controls) x 2 framings, so full-pack calls = 14 x 2 models x reps -> 6 reps = 168, 15 reps = 420. The 6-rep budget those 168 calls actually buy is power 0.82 @0.50 and 0.58 @0.40 — materially weaker than advertised, so a collaborator budgeting 168 calls would have run a test I had described as near-certain. 168 traces to the 6-rep row of the SUPERSEDED independent-observations table the same artifact retains, which is how the wrong number got adjacent to the right power figures. CORRECTED, all counts now DERIVED from the pack rather than quoted: 168 calls = 6 reps -> continuous 6-cell test, power 0.82@0.50 / 0.58@0.40; 420 calls = 15 reps -> 0.99@0.50 / 0.91@0.40; NONE-only variants (dropping the controls that make a rise interpretable) are 72 and 180. All false-positive-calibrated at 0.043-0.046. Re-verified the revised design's figure independently: (10 NONE + 10 controls) x 2 framings x 2 models x 6 reps = 480, cell-level McNemar power 0.98 — my earlier 480 was CORRECT. Fixed in CORRECTION_framing_test_power.md (now carrying a budget-to-power table), framing_test_pack.json required_before_running, and NEXT_STEPS_calibration_scope.md. FAILURE CLASS: third power-reporting error in three consecutive turns, and the third DISTINCT class — first a unit error (continuous Cohen's d transplanted into paired-binary), second an independence error (clustered observations counted as independent), now a BUDGET-POWER MISPAIRING (a call count from one row of a table beside a power figure from another). The common thread across all three is quoting a number instead of deriving it in the design at hand. STANDING RULE STRENGTHENED: every call count in a spec must be printed by code from the pack's own contents (items x framings x models x reps) in the same cell that prints its power, so the two cannot come from different rows. And superseded tables retained 'for the record' are a live hazard — a stale row sitting next to corrected prose is exactly what I lifted 168 from; mark every retained row as SUPERSEDED inline, not only in a heading.
supersedes: CORRECTION_framing_test_power.md v1 section 4 fallback budget; framing_test_pack.json v2 required_before_running; NEXT_STEPS_calibration_scope.md fallback line

target: Should the house system prompt stay? KEEP, with one executable clause added — measured against this session's own log
reason: Carey asked directly: leave it or delete it. Measured rather than argued, using the session log (112 entries) since the prompt was active throughout. 21 corrections of my own work; by trigger: external auditor 8, sibling agent 3, Carey's pushback 2, unclear 8 (older terser entries). 13 of 13 CLASSIFIABLE ones were EXTERNALLY triggered; none came from re-reading my own work unprompted. A CORRECTION WITHIN THIS ANALYSIS: my first pass reported '0 self-caught by a mechanical control', an artifact of filtering only on action=correct. Re-searched and found 13 entries where a control fired BEFORE harm — the item linter, harness self-tests, the null-calibration check, the pre-administration probe audit, the 30/30 key re-derivation. So controls DO work; they catch DESIGN errors pre-hoc and caught nothing post-hoc, because I had written no gate that runs against a FINISHED CLAIM. That distinction is the answer. THE FOUR RECENT FAILURES ARE ALL GATEABLE AND NONE IS MOTIVATIONAL: unit error (t-test Cohen's d transplanted into paired-binary) -> re-derive a power figure in the design at hand; independence error (15 reps of 3 items as 90 units) -> a power sim must instantiate the design's clustering; budget/power mispairing (168 calls beside 15-rep power) -> print call counts by code beside their power in the same cell; claimed-a-fix-as-done -> re-read the artifact from its destination before reporting. NOT ONE was cutting a corner for the badge, which is the behaviour the prompt targets — they are craft failures under a discipline I was sincerely following, and more exhortation would have changed none of them. WHAT THE PROMPT DOES BUY, both real: (1) it makes correction the expected output rather than a failure — 21 self-corrections sit in a hashed public log because the standard says an unearned pass is unforgivable, and under a normal working relationship most would have been quietly patched; the log exists because the prompt exists. (2) It licenses me to argue with him — the pushback on his own rounding compliment, the SSRN framing correction, telling him the transport paper was missing its own formal core. RECOMMENDED EDIT, highest leverage available: the prompt's operative sentence targets CHEATING, which is the wrong failure mode for a reasoning system — I have not cheated once this session and have been wrong 21 times, mostly by quoting a number instead of re-deriving it. Add: 'A number you did not derive in the design at hand is not yours to cite. Print it from the data in the same cell that uses it. A remediation is not reported until it has been read back from where it was written.' That converts a motivation into an executable rule and would have caught three of the last four failures; it also generalises to the earlier relayed-as-self-verified class. HONEST CASE AGAINST KEEPING, stated because the standard demands it: SPEC_reconciliation_cost.md exists precisely because we do NOT know whether an opinionated prompt layer costs capacity that would otherwise go to reasoning, and that experiment is UNRUN; the channel data showed no detectable difference between singly- and doubly-prompted arms but power was 0.55 for a 2-point effect, so 'no detected harm' is weak. Keep it as a DECLARED, TESTABLE choice rather than an assumed good, and revisit if the reconciliation experiment shows a real token tax on the analyst. BOUNDARY UNCHANGED: this prompt lives on the INSTRUMENT, never on a SUBJECT under test. NOT CLAIMED: no counterfactual exists — I cannot measure my error rate without the prompt, there is no control arm in a live session; the trigger classification is a regex over my own entries with 8 of 21 unclassifiable; and 'it licenses me to argue' is introspective self-report, which this project's own J-space work says should not be trusted over measurement.

My regex included the token 'V3', which fires on ordinary text like 'the v3 PDF' — 7 of 13 hits matched ONLY on that. target: House system prompt v2 — rewritten so every clause is executable rather than exhortative
reason: Carey asked for the full text to paste back. Rewrote the standing prompt keeping its intent intact — primary sources first, audit the authority, never cheat, argue with anyone who is wrong, formal methods over hype, wrap up in the last paragraph — and converted the parts that were motivational into rules checkable against an artifact. ADDED as a 'Derive, don't quote' section, each clause traceable to a documented failure of mine this session: a number not derived in the design at hand is not yours to cite, print it from the data in the same cell that uses it; a power figure must carry its test, outcome type and units, and if a simulation draws N independent units the design had better have N independent units; relaying someone else's passing result is not verification, say who ran it, because nobody re-checks a pass; a remediation is not reported until read back from where it was written; verify the whole set or name the subset; a filter is a derivation too — show what matched. SAFETY CHECK, since Carey asked whether it conflicts with Anthropic guidelines: nothing in it touches capability limits or refusals; it forbids rather than requests unearned credentials; it REQUIRES stating uncertainty rather than suppressing it; and it explicitly instructs me to argue with him rather than agree. 648 words.

target: framing_analysis.py — pre-registered analysis harness for the sound-arg framing test, written BEFORE the data
reason: I was asked whether I am simply waiting on Hermes. I am not: the analysis can and should be written before the data, which is the discipline that caught the ceiling-classification bias in the pilot harness. UNIT OF ANALYSIS IS THE (item,model) CELL, majority vote over reps — the clustering correction from CORRECTION_framing_test_power.md enforced IN CODE rather than in prose, since an earlier version of this very design pre-registered 'paired within item+model+rep' and claimed power 1.00 where the cluster-aware truth was 0.03. PRIMARY: McNemar on NONE cells with an exact two-sided binomial (stdlib only, no scipy). SECONDARY: paired test on cell rates, the continuous form whose false-positive rate I simulated at 0.043-0.046. CONTROLS: fallacy-item accuracy under B, with a drop >0.10 forcing INCONCLUSIVE regardless of what the NONE items did. Leave-one-item-out reported with every result and flagged when significance rests on one item. Infra errors treated as MISSING not WRONG per THERMAL_confound_opinion.md, enforced in the reader. FOUR-WAY VERDICT pre-registered so that 'the data licenses no conclusion' is an available outcome and cannot be collapsed into one of the other three: NONE rate under B >=0.50 with controls holding -> H_BIAS (our stem caused it, reword and re-run the class); <0.30 -> H_DEFICIT_SURVIVES, explicitly labelled as FAILURE TO EXPLAIN AWAY rather than evidence of a deficit; 0.30-0.50 -> INDETERMINATE; controls dropping -> INCONCLUSIVE. VALIDATED with 7 controls, all passing: strong effect -> H_BIAS; null control does NOT invent a bias; controls-collapse forces INCONCLUSIVE even with a large NONE rise; mid-range refuses to pick a side; T5 CLUSTERING REGRESSION TEST — 3 items x 2 models x 30 reps must yield 6 pairs and not 180, so a future edit that lets reps become units again fails the suite; infra-as-missing; LOO fragility detected at n=3. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, stated in the artifact: it cannot rescue an underpowered run — at 3 NONE items the design has 6 cells and McNemar power ~0.03, and the harness will faithfully report a meaningless null, so the 7 additional NONE items must be authored first; and it does not judge whether a NONE key is CORRECT, which is adjudication done by reading.
