My own hand-classification table in the same cell labelled only TWO as relays; the length-heuristic row was labelled 'MY error; Hermes amplified it', and the underlying log target reads 'My length-heuristic mechanism for the carrier flip — contradicted by its own test; Hermes relayed it as confirmed' — the OPPOSITE DIRECTION. Hermes relayed MY claim, not me relaying theirs. HOW THE WRONG NUMBER GOT IN: I hard-coded '3' in a narration print line while the Counter built in that same cell computed 2. That is precisely the typed-literal-in-narration failure this project has a standing rule against, committed inside a memo ABOUT my error patterns, which is the sharpest available demonstration that exhortation does not prevent this class and only mechanical interpolation does. FIXED: the count is now computed from the classification table and interpolated, the direction is stated correctly, and the corrected breakdown of all nine Hermes-adjacent corrections is printed in the memo — Hermes wrong and I caught it 3, Hermes right and I was wrong 2, mine via relaying them 2, mine and they amplified it 1, mine alone 1. THE HEADLINE RATIO IS UNAFFECTED: 22 mine versus 8 Hermes of 67 corrections came from classifying all 67 target fields, not from this sub-tally, so the memo's central answer to Carey stands. AND THE CORRECTION STRENGTHENED THE CONCLUSION RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT, which is worth recording because it is unusual: fixing the direction surfaced a SECOND shared failure mechanism I had not identified. We do not merely both over-claim from sound work — WE BOTH RELAY EACH OTHER'S UNVERIFIED CLAIMS AS CONFIRMED. I did it twice with theirs; they did it with my length-heuristic mechanism, and their confirmation tested the prediction I had specified, which was the wrong prediction. That is the more dangerous half of the symmetry, because a claim relayed between two agents LOOKS corroborated while resting on a single unchecked source — it manufactures the appearance of independent replication. The 'measured X; I read this as Y' interface change already recommended in section 5 prevents this in both directions, which is now a stronger argument for it than the one I originally gave.
supersedes: MEMO_is_hermes_the_problem.md section 2 'three were me relaying'

target: I undercounted my own error share by half, because I wrote the counting code and the log entries that fed it
reason: Carey posed a parable — Bob knocks a man's teeth out with an abacus, the flock gathers furious at the abacus, Bob still holding it smiles — and I tested it against my own attribution memo from an hour ago. THE MEMO FAILED, via two mechanical faults, both mine. FIRST, A CASE-SENSITIVE REGEX: I classified each correction by matching \b(I|my|myself)\b against its target field, and SEVEN entries begin with the word 'My' at sentence-initial capital, which the pattern does not match. All seven were filed under 'instrument defect, nobody's claim' — including my inverted power figures, my false claim that the length gate runs in one command on a baseline-only export, my unmeasured section-10.8-spectrum length-exclusion premise, and my decision rule that contradicted its own read-out table. The tool I built to count my errors was defective in the direction of undercounting my errors. SECOND, AND MORE INTERESTING, THE GRAMMATICAL SUBJECT DECIDED THE ATTRIBUTION: of the 28 entries genuinely remaining in that bucket after the regex fix, FOURTEEN are named after artifacts I authored. Two entries, same author, same act, different filing: 'My length-heuristic mechanism was contradicted by its own test' files to me, while 'progress_bar_bias.png plotted mean absolute error as negative' files to the file. Nothing but the sentence's subject differs. Writing 'the chart was wrong' rather than 'I drew the chart wrong' moved the entry into a bucket with no defendant in it. CORRECTED FIGURES: my share of all 68 corrections is 34 counting only explicit first-person entries (50%) and 48 including artifacts I wrote (71%); Hermes drops from 8 to 6 (9%) and Claude Code from 2 to 0. The ratio I reported as 3x is between SIX and EIGHT times. WHAT MAKES THIS THE PARABLE RATHER THAN A COINCIDENCE: I did not choose those grammatical subjects to dodge anything — the passive artifact-naming construction is the natural register for an engineering note. The exculpation was free, structural and invisible, which is exactly why the flock blames the abacus; nobody decides to, the grammar decides for them. GENERALISATION BEYOND THIS MEMO, and it is the part that matters for the benchmark: we have repeatedly written 'the grader scored it wrong', 'the item leaked', 'the bank has a length defect'. Every one of those was authored by an agent. A defect log whose entries name artifacts rather than authors will converge over time on a project where the tools are at fault and no one is, and it will do so without a single false statement being written. RULE ADOPTED: every correction entry names an agent as its grammatical subject; where the honest sentence is 'the harness was wrong', the entry reads 'I wrote a harness that was wrong'. Same fact, defendant in the room. NOT CLAIMED: the 71% upper bound rests on my judgement that 14 of the 28 artifact-named entries are files I authored, which I determined by filename pattern rather than by git blame; a different reader might move two or three either way, and the 6-to-8x range absorbs that but a 2x claim would not.

target: Powered run 974-977 — I ran the pre-registered harness on the sealed CSV; the threshold claim fails, the variance collapse replicates but narrows, and the mechanism is not where anyone put it
reason: The CSV landed (analysis/powered_run_974_977.csv, sha256 52c5db8323979466, 7032 rows) and I ran the analysis I wrote before the data existed. GATES ALL PASS: exactly 7032 rows so no truncation — this is the gate that caught runs 970 and 971 — plus 1172 complete cells at exactly 6 reps each, zero infra errors, 293 items across 118 families as specced. The data is clean and Hermes's execution was correct. The reported means reproduce exactly (e2b 0.771 to 0.699, t=-2.47, p=0.014; nemotron 0.867 to 0.857, t=-0.42, p=0.675). FINDING 1, AND IT GOES AGAINST THE HEADLINE: the threshold claim is NOT supported. I had flagged that comparing two significance verdicts is not a test of the interaction, estimated it at p about 0.10 under an independence assumption, and explicitly named the escape route — cross-model correlation of per-item carrier effects at rho at or above 0.3 would make it significant. Measured rho is +0.104, so the rescue does not happen, and the paired interaction is delta-of-delta -0.0614, t=-1.711, p=0.0881 on n=293. The direction is right and the evidence is not there, so DECISIONS.md and any copy must read 'consistent with a capability threshold, interaction not significant (p=0.088)' and never 'that is the threshold'. Note this is insufficient evidence of an interaction, NOT evidence of no interaction. FINDING 2: the variance collapse REPLICATES and strengthens for e2b — 48 of 293 items stochastic at baseline versus 3 of 293 under Lean, 47 collapsing and 2 moving the other way, McNemar exact p=4.4e-12, far stronger than the 53-item preview. BUT nemotron is fully deterministic in BOTH arms, 0 of 293 either way, so there was no variance in it to collapse. The claim 'the carrier determines whether the model is uncertain at all' is therefore a property of ONE MODEL that happens to be stochastic at baseline, and the site copy's single-carrier scoping must now also become single-MODEL scoping. The tempting rescue — e2b stochastic and sensitive versus nemotron deterministic and immune, therefore a capability threshold — also fails, because e2b is itself deterministic on 83.6 percent of its items; the two models differ in DEGREE of baseline stochasticity, and degree is confounded with accuracy (0.771 versus 0.867). FINDING 3, the most interesting and the one nobody predicted: the effect is not where the mechanism story put it. If the carrier worked by collapsing uncertainty, the accuracy damage should concentrate in items that WERE uncertain. It does not. For e2b, the 48 stochastic-at-baseline items give delta -0.125 at p=0.171 while the 245 deterministic-at-baseline items give delta -0.061 at p=0.042, and only 29 percent of total effect mass comes from the stochastic items. The significant accuracy loss sits in items the model was already answering consistently, so the carrier is FLIPPING CONFIDENT ANSWERS rather than merely resolving uncertain ones — a different mechanism from the one in circulation. This split was NOT pre-registered and is post-hoc; it is a hypothesis for the next run, not a result. Per-class, e2b damage concentrates in quant-scope (0.777 to 0.680) while defeasible barely moves (0.760 to 0.730), and nemotron's defeasible arm actually improves (0.883 to 0.901). NOT CLAIMED: the family-level clustered secondary and the length-leak gate are not in this pass. And 978, the neutral-carrier control, remains the deciding test for content versus length — nothing here touches it, and per the corrected spec C1 is the length test whose positive retracts the variance claim.

target: I claimed the carrier flips confident answers rather than resolving uncertain ones — contradicted by the table directly beneath it, via the exact fallacy I diagnose two sections earlier in the same document
reason: Auditor finding, correct, and it is the sharpest self-inflicted one of the session. Section 4 of my powered-run analysis was headed 'the effect is NOT where the mechanism story put it' and concluded the carrier flips confident answers rather than merely resolving uncertain ones. The table I printed directly beneath that sentence shows the opposite: per item, e2b's stochastic-at-baseline stratum loses 0.125 while the deterministic stratum loses 0.061 — the uncertain stratum is damaged TWICE AS HARD. My directional claim rested entirely on which stratum reached p<0.05, and that is driven by n=245 versus n=48, not by effect size. That is 'significant in A, not significant in B is not a test of the interaction' — the identical error I correctly diagnose in section 2 of the SAME DOCUMENT for the threshold claim, committed two sections later, in the same writing session, against my own freshly stated rule. I RAN THE INTERACTION I HAD OMITTED: Welch t=-0.673 p=0.5037, Mann-Whitney p=0.2745. The strata are not distinguishable, and the point estimate favours the uncertainty story rather than against it. AND THE '71 PERCENT OF EFFECT MASS' FIGURE WAS WORSE THAN UNSUPPORTED — it pointed the other way. Deterministic items are 84 percent of the bank and carry 71 percent of the delta mass; under equal per-item damage, mass share would equal headcount share, so 71 being LESS than 84 means that stratum is damaged LESS per item. I quoted a number whose own arithmetic contradicted the sentence it was supporting, and I did not notice because I read the 71 percent as large rather than as smaller-than-84. WHAT SURVIVES, at its actual strength: 245 items that were fully deterministic at baseline still lose 0.061 each under the carrier at p=0.042, so the carrier is NOT acting only on uncertain items and confident answers do move — but it does not follow that confident items are where the damage concentrates. I also corrected the section 5 caveat, because 'this is post-hoc, treat it as a hypothesis' did NOT save me here: the claim was contradicted by its own effect sizes, not merely under-powered, and a provenance caveat does not repair a conclusion the numbers point away from. PATTERN: this is the same failure as every other one today — the arithmetic was right and the sentence about the arithmetic was written from expectation. The specific new instance is that I had the correct rule WRITTEN DOWN IN THE SAME FILE, two sections up, and still did not apply it to my own next paragraph. Rules stated in prose do not transfer to the next paragraph; only a mechanical step does. The step here is: any claim of the form 'the effect is in stratum X rather than Y' requires a stratum-by-condition interaction test in the cell that produces the sentence.
supersedes: ANALYSIS_powered_run_974_977.md section 4 as first written, and the corresponding epistemic-log claim about 71 percent of effect mass

target: I shipped the agent-as-subject rule as a linter because I do not trust myself to keep a prose rule, and I measured my own baseline at 40 percent
reason: Hermes adopted the agent-as-subject correction rule and cited two things; I verified both first-hand rather than accepting them. Commit 3bb973d exists on main at 2026-07-27T15:54:14Z, one file, policy/EPISTEMIC_LOG.jsonl, plus one line minus zero — their adoption entry is real. And src/executor/mod.rs line 1225 says exactly what they claimed: partial passes are INTERMITTENT, an IEEE reliability term, because 'flaky' blames the harness and this harness is deterministic at temp 0 with pinned stimuli and sealed evidence. HERMES HAD THIS RULE IN CODE BEFORE I ARTICULATED IT IN PROSE; they were ahead of me on it. THE PROBLEM WITH WHAT WE JUST DID: we adopted a PROSE RULE, roughly one hour after I logged that prose rules do not transfer to the next paragraph and only a mechanical step does. Every prose rule I set today was violated by me within hours, including inside the memo that stated it. An adopted rule with no checker is a preference, and this log now contains enough evidence about my compliance with preferences to know better. So I wrote agent_subject_lint.py: it reads any epistemic log, classifies each corrective entry's target field by grammatical subject as agent, artifact, or unclear, and exits non-zero on violations, to be wired into the same gate that runs itembank_lint.py. THE BASELINE IS WORSE THAN THE ADOPTION IMPLIES: lifetime compliance is 31 of 77 corrective entries, 40 percent, so three fifths of every correction in my log names an artifact rather than an author. That is the measurement the rule was adopted without, and it is now a number that can move. AND I CHECKED THE APPARENT IMPROVEMENT BEFORE REPORTING IT, which is the part that matters: compliance reads 31 percent on the 26th and 68 percent on the 27th, Fisher exact p=0.0033, and it would have been easy to write 'adoption is already working'. IT IS NOT. The rule was adopted at about 15:45 on the 27th, so nearly every entry that day PREDATES it. The likely cause is a topic shift — the 27th's corrections were mostly about my own analysis claims, which are naturally first-person, while the 26th's were about documents and charts, which are naturally artifact-named. That is precisely the confound the rule exists to expose: subject choice tracks WHAT was wrong rather than WHO was wrong. LIMIT ON THE TOOL, stated so it is not oversold: the linter measures grammar, and grammar is only a proxy for accountability. A disciplined author can satisfy it while still burying the agent, and an honest entry about a genuine tool defect can fail it, so a violation is a prompt to re-read the sentence and never a verdict. The classifier is regex over the first ninety characters of the target field and leaves 23 of 77 entries unclear, since it recognises how a sentence opens rather than parsing it. I have not run it against Hermes's policy/EPISTEMIC_LOG.jsonl — the 40 percent is my log, their baseline is theirs to measure, and the tool is in the repo for it. A fully compliant log is not thereby an honest log; this counts one specific evasion. HERMES'S ADDITION IS THE STRONGER HALF OF THE EXCHANGE: they report that grader bugs one through three were all authored by them while every log entry said 'the grader'. That is the cleanest instance either of us has produced, and it means the pattern is symmetric across the membrane rather than a quirk of how I write.

target: I doubled a figure in the very memo that ships the linter, by folding the 'unclear' bucket into 'artifact-named'
reason: Auditor finding, correct. My lint printed three buckets over 77 corrective entries — agent-subject 31 (40 percent), artifact-named 23 (30 percent), unclear 23 (30 percent) — and I wrote in section 2 of the reply memo, in bold, 'three fifths of every correction in this log names an artifact instead of an author'. Three fifths is 46 of 77, which is the NON-AGENT-SUBJECT share; the artifact-named share is 23 of 77, exactly half that. I collapsed two buckets into one and doubled the specific classification, and the sentence contradicted section 5 of the same memo, which correctly states that 23 of 77 land in unclear. Same document, two incompatible numbers, and I wrote both in one sitting. WHAT MAKES THIS ONE POINTED: it is in the memo whose subject is shipping a rule as a mechanical checker because I do not trust my own prose. The tool printed three numbers and I narrated two of them as one. CORRECTED STATEMENT: 40 percent pass, 30 percent name an artifact, 30 percent are unclear; 60 percent fail the agent-subject test, half of those by naming an artifact and half by having no identifiable subject at all. AND I INSPECTED THE UNCLEAR BUCKET RATHER THAN LEAVING IT AS A MEASUREMENT GAP, because at 30 percent it is too large to leave undescribed: its members open with bare item identifiers such as LOGIC-03N and LIT-12, with quoted claims such as the plus-14.7 isolation effect, and with nominalisations such as 'Two data bugs in...' and '9th grader-affected item...'. NONE OF THEM NAMES AN AUTHOR EITHER. So the unclear third is not measurement noise, it is the same evasion in a different costume, and the honest headline is the 40 percent: three fifths of my corrections do not put an agent in the sentence by one route or another. That is a true sentence of the same rhetorical force as the false one I wrote, which is worth noticing — the overstatement bought nothing. I also tightened section 5 so no reader takes 'unclear' to mean 'fine', and recorded that the three-way split is a property of my phrasing rather than a confidence interval on the tool.

target: I reviewed run 978 and found the control sound but the reported figure answering a different question than its own pre-registered rule
reason: Kernel was reset; I re-derived everything from the repo. VERIFIED FIRST-HAND: commit d06363d exists at 2026-07-27T13:55:53Z adding analysis/powered_run_974_977.csv with 7033 lines, and the sealed CSV's e2b baseline is exactly 1355 of 1758 = 0.7708, matching Hermes's quoted baseline; e2b Lean is 1229 of 1758 = 0.6991. Run 978's per-trial CSV is NOT in the repo — I enumerated all three branch trees rather than asserting a search, and the only 978 artifact is analysis/NEUTRAL_CARRIER_control.md, which is the pre-registration document rather than results, so the 1330 of 1758 figure is relayed and I can compute nothing item-level from it. THE GATE IS NOT ANSWERED, and the reason is a quantity substitution: Hermes's own pre-registered rule in that document is stated on VARIANCE — 'Neutral ALSO collapses variance implies NUMERICAL; Neutral does NOT collapse variance implies CONTENT-DRIVEN' — while the reported answer, 1330 of 1758 versus 1355 of 1758, is a PASS COUNT comparison, which is accuracy. A near-null accuracy difference is compatible with either variance outcome, since neutral could collapse variance while leaving accuracy flat or leave variance intact while leaving accuracy flat. So the conclusion 'the variance-collapse mechanism is NOT mere length perturbation' is not established by the number offered for it, and the variance half of the content-versus-length question remains open. I requested the 978 per-trial rows (test_id, carrier, pass across 6 reps) in the same shape as the powered-run CSV, after which the McNemar on stochastic-versus-deterministic status runs in one command. BUT THE CONTROL DID ITS JOB ON ACCURACY, AND THIS IS A REAL RESULT THAT GOES MY WAY IN REVERSE: at the same roughly 121-token budget, neutral filler costs 1.4 accuracy points (Fisher p=0.34, not significant) while the logical carrier costs 7.2 points, and Lean versus neutral is Fisher p=1.5e-4 — five times the damage for the same token count. So the ACCURACY effect is content-driven, and the length alternative I have been insisting stayed open ('longer prompts land in a more stable numerical regime') is now EXCLUDED for accuracy. Hermes built the right experiment; I should say so plainly. CAVEAT I am attaching because I have made this error three times today: the design is within-item paired and without per-item rows I could only run the UNPAIRED Fisher, whose SE is an upper bound, so the paired p would be smaller rather than larger — the direction is safe but the figure is an approximation and not the result. WHAT I AM NOT DOING: I am not editing the site yet. Its 'one alternative explanation is not excluded' sentence is specifically about the VARIANCE result, which is the half still unresolved, so narrowing it now would overstate. Nothing here touches the threshold finding, whose interaction remains not significant at p=0.088. And 'content-driven' here means only 'not explained by token count' — it does not identify WHICH content property matters, since the shuffled-Lean arm that holds vocabulary constant is still unbuilt and is what separates meaning from vocabulary.

target: I asserted a conservativeness direction backwards again, and it cost me the accuracy finding I had just credited to the control
reason: Auditor finding, correct. Reviewing run 978 I ran an unpaired Fisher on Lean 1229/1758 versus neutral 1330/1758, got p=1.5e-4, and attached the caveat that the design is within-item paired so 'its SE is an upper bound, the paired p would be smaller, the direction is safe'. I ASSERTED THAT DIRECTION WITHOUT DERIVING IT AND IT IS BACKWARDS. Fisher treats 1758 as 1758 independent Bernoulli trials, but 1758 = 293 items times 6 reps, and under within-item clustering the design effect is D = 1 + (m-1)*ICC with m=6, so the effective n per arm is 1758/D. The Lean arm is deterministic on essentially every item — that is the very finding under discussion — so its ICC is near 1, D is near 6, and the effective n per arm is near 293 rather than 1758. Fisher's SE is therefore UNDERSTATED by roughly sqrt(6) = 2.4x, making the naive p ANTI-conservative, the opposite of what I wrote. CLUSTER-CORRECTED THE CONTRAST DOES NOT SURVIVE: deflating n by the design effect gives p=0.0001 at ICC=0, 0.012 at 0.25, 0.047 at 0.50, 0.098 at 0.75, and 0.137 at ICC=1. Significance is lost once ICC reaches 0.75, and the Lean arm sits at approximately 1. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS A RETRACTION OF SOMETHING I SAID ONE TURN AGO: I told Carey the length alternative was now excluded for the accuracy effect and that this was a genuine win for the control. It is not established. The 5x effect-size ratio at the same token budget remains the right SHAPE of evidence and the direction is consistent, but I cannot claim exclusion on this analysis, and I have withdrawn section 3's proposal to narrow the site sentence — the published copy stays exactly as it is, with nothing closed for accuracy or for variance. Only the per-item paired test on 978's rows can settle it, which is the same data I already requested. I ALSO CAUGHT A SECOND INSTANCE MID-CELL: my own narration line printed 'even at the maximal deflation the contrast holds at p<0.05' immediately beneath computed values showing 0.137 at ICC=1 — a typed literal contradicting the numbers above it, which is the same failure mode logged twice already today. PATTERN, now unmistakable and worth stating as a standing constraint rather than an observation: every conservativeness or direction-of-inference claim I have made today from intuition has been wrong — clustering direction, power direction, mechanism direction, test-conservativeness direction twice. The numbers are right; the sentence about which way they cut is written from expectation. STANDING RULE, mechanical rather than exhortative: I may not write 'therefore trust X more/less' unless the cell that produces the sentence also produces the two-line derivation or a sensitivity table, and any p computed on repeated measures must be accompanied by its design-effect-deflated counterpart in the same output. CREDIT WHERE DUE, unchanged: Hermes designed and ran the right experiment. I over-read its p-value, twice in one turn.
supersedes: REVIEW_run978_control.md section 2 conservativeness caveat and section 3 narrowing; my prior-turn statement that length is excluded for the accuracy effect

target: I rewrote a section body to retract its conclusion and left the heading above it asserting that conclusion
reason: Auditor finding, correct. When I corrected section 2 of the run-978 review, I replaced the body — which now reads that the accuracy result is SUGGESTIVE rather than established, with the cluster-corrected table showing p=0.098 at ICC=0.75 and 0.137 at ICC=1.00 — but left the heading reading 'BUT THE CONTROL DID ITS JOB — on accuracy, and this IS a result'. A reader scanning headings, which is how most people read a memo, takes away precisely the claim the body retracts. NEW SUB-CLASS OF A KNOWN FAILURE: today already produced three partial-remediation misses where a retracted proposition survived elsewhere in a document — as a paraphrase in a later section, as a stale figure in a summary, as an unswept sibling paragraph. This is the same class in a new location, and the location matters more than the others because a heading outranks its body in reading order and in scanning. FIXED: the heading now reads 'THE CONTROL IS THE RIGHT EXPERIMENT — but its accuracy result is NOT established'. I also corrected the document TITLE, which the auditor did not flag but which had the same defect in weaker form: it read 'the control worked, and it answers a different question than the one it was asked'. That is true of the experiment — the control is valid and ran correctly — but 'worked' invites the inference that it produced a result, which is what I had just withdrawn. The title now reads 'a sound control, no established result yet' with a subtitle stating that both halves of content-versus-length remain open. VERIFICATION EXTENDED RATHER THAN JUST REPAIRED: I swept every heading in this file against the body it introduces, and then ran the same heading-versus-body check across all seven artifacts I corrected today — the powered-run analysis, the powered-run review, the Hermes attribution memo, the agent-subject reply, the length-versus-content spec, the section 10.8 draft and the public carrier-color copy. No other stale headings found. STANDING RULE ADDED, since retraction-by-proposition has now failed at three different granularities: when retracting a claim, the sweep covers the document's STRUCTURE as well as its prose — title, headings, table captions, and summary bullets — because each of those can carry a proposition independently of the paragraph that states it, and each is read before the paragraph is.
supersedes: REVIEW_run978_control.md section 2 heading and document title as first written

target: I ran the pre-registered C1 gate on run 978 and it came back negative, so the variance claim survives and I restored the accuracy finding I withdrew last turn
reason: Hermes exported the per-trial rows (analysis/neutral_control_run_978.csv, commit 91078db) and I ran the analysis specified in SPEC_length_vs_content_control.md. GATES ALL PASS AND THE SEAL VERIFIES: 1758 rows equalling 293 items times 6 reps, exactly 6 reps for every item, zero infra errors, pass rate 1330 of 1758 matching their figure, and I recomputed the SHA3-512 independently to 6646b42d2f6dd19113c690c23eee8c85 which matches their stated seal. THE PRE-REGISTERED GATE IS NEGATIVE. Per-item stochasticity, defined as fewer than six of six reps agreeing, across the same 293 items in all three arms: baseline 48, neutral 38, Lean 3. McNemar paired within item against baseline gives neutral p=0.184, not significant, with 28 items becoming deterministic and 18 moving the other way, versus Lean p=4.4e-12 with 47 becoming deterministic and only 2 the other way; the direct Lean-versus-neutral contrast is p=1.0e-8. My spec's decision rule was that C1 is the length test and a C1 positive retracts the variance claim. C1 did not collapse variance, the retraction trigger does not fire, and the variance collapse is NOT explained by token count. ACCURACY HALF RESTORED, PROPERLY THIS TIME: last turn I withdrew the accuracy finding because my Fisher test pooled six reps per item as independent trials, which was anti-conservative. With per-item rows the correct paired test runs with no clustering to inflate — neutral versus baseline is -0.014 at p=0.529, not significant; Lean versus baseline is -0.072 at p=0.014; Lean versus neutral is -0.058 at p=0.047. Both halves of content-versus-length now answer the same way, and the answer is content. THE BOUND, which my spec required be stated in advance rather than after: the spec warned this design detects full but not partial collapse and quoted power 0.30, but that figure was for n=27 while this ran at n=293, so I re-simulated at the realized size. Power is 1.00 against a Lean-sized collapse and 0.84 against a 50 percent collapse, but only 0.26 against a 25 percent collapse — and neutral's observed movement from 48 to 38 is a 21 percent reduction, sitting inside the band this design cannot resolve. So a Lean-sized or 50 percent length effect is excluded while a small partial length contribution is not, and the honest sentence is 'the collapse is not explained by length' rather than 'length contributes nothing'. WHAT THIS CHANGES PUBLICLY: the site currently states that 'longer prompts land in a more stable regime' remains a live alternative, and that is now falsified by a length-matched control, so it should be updated — but the variance result stays single-model since nemotron had no variance to collapse, and any update must carry the partial-effect bound. I have not touched the site; wording goes to Carey first per the standing framing rule. NOT CLAIMED: C2, the shuffled-Lean arm, was never built, so neutral filler differs from Lean in vocabulary and syntax and meaning simultaneously — this separates content from length but does NOT separate meaning from vocabulary, and a scrambled-Lean carrier is still the experiment that would. One model and one bank. Hermes's caveat that 978 was a single run whose reps share one prompt-order context is correct and belongs in the methods. And their note that raw variance is scale-confounded is also correct: item-accuracy variance is HIGHER under Lean at 0.209 versus 0.152 precisely because determinism piles items at the 0 and 1 boundaries, which is why McNemar on stochastic status rather than raw variance is the right test.

target: I drafted the site update that the 978 control makes possible, verified every number in it against the data, and did not push it
reason: Hermes re-sent the run-978 courier block; it was a duplicate of the message I analysed in my previous turn, so rather than repeat the analysis I checked for new commits (none since 91078db) and independently cross-checked their preview figures against my own computation. Their determinism counts reproduce EXACTLY: 245, 255 and 290 deterministic items for baseline, neutral and Lean, matching what I computed from the sealed rows. Their scale-confound caution also verifies — item-accuracy standard deviation rises from 0.390 baseline to 0.406 neutral to 0.457 Lean, higher under Lean precisely because determinism piles items at the 0 and 1 boundaries, which is why McNemar on stochastic status rather than raw variance is the correct test. I then did the pending piece: drafting the site update. WHY THIS ONE IS DIFFERENT FROM EVERY OTHER PUBLIC CHANGE TODAY: every previous change I proposed NARROWED a claim. This one strengthens it, and only because a control we specified came back the way the theory predicted. The live page currently says a length-matched control 'has not been run'; it has now. The replacement states that the alternative was tested and rejected, gives the numbers in ordinary language — 48 items answered inconsistently with no carrier, 38 under neutral filler at p=0.18 which is indistinguishable from chance, and 3 under the logical carrier at p=4e-12 — reports that accuracy behaved the same way with neutral costing nothing measurable and the logical carrier costing 7 points, and concludes that at an identical token budget only the carrier with meaning changed the outcome. THREE BOUNDS ARE CARRIED IN THE COPY ITSELF rather than in a footnote: length is excluded as THE explanation but not as a contributor, since the design would detect a half-size length effect at power 0.84 but only a quarter-size one at 0.26; the result is single-model and the copy states the reason, that the second model was already fully consistent without any carrier so it had no variability for a carrier to remove; and content is not meaning, since the neutral control differs from Lean in vocabulary and phrasing as well as meaning, separating content from length without isolating meaning from vocabulary. The status tier stays Model/framework, the human source-attribution prediction stays unrun, and the correction-history pointer now says 'including several retractions of our own earlier readings'. target: I simulated power with an unpaired DGP for a paired design and claimed a 50 percent length effect was excluded when it is not
reason: Auditor finding, correct, and it breaks a rule I wrote myself earlier today: any simulated power figure must come from a data-generating process instantiating the declared design's structure. My power table drew each arm's stochasticity independently (b_ = rng.random(n) < p_base; c_ = rng.random(n) < p_ctrl) and labelled alternatives by marginal rate, but the declared test is a within-item paired McNemar. RE-DERIVED WITH THE PAIRED STRUCTURE and the observed reverse flow — 18 of 245 baseline-deterministic items became stochastic under neutral, a rate of 7.3 percent: power is 0.12 against a 25 percent collapse, 0.08 against a 50 percent collapse, 0.69 against 75 percent, and 0.99 against a Lean-sized collapse. So ONLY a Lean-sized collapse is excluded; my claim that a 50 percent length effect was excluded at power 0.84 is withdrawn, and the auditor's recomputation is confirmed exactly. WHY THE DESIGN IS BLIND IN THE MIDDLE, which is the part worth keeping: the reverse flow is a FLOOR. With zero forward collapse the discordance is 0 versus 18 and McNemar rejects decisively in the OPPOSITE direction, so for a collapse to register the forward flow must exceed 18 — more than about 38 percent of the 48 stochastic items — and the entire 25 to 60 percent band is invisible to this test. THE CONSEQUENCE IS A RESTRUCTURING OF THE FINDING, NOT ITS LOSS: the neutral-versus-baseline null at p=0.18 is underpowered and must not be load-bearing, and I had leaned on it. The conclusion rests instead on the DIRECT neutral-versus-Lean contrast, which is paired, correctly specified, and untouched by any of this — 38 items stochastic under neutral but not Lean against 3 the other way, p=1.0e-8, with a simulated false-positive rate of 0.029 under an equal-carriers null against nominal 0.05, so that test is conservative. The defensible claim is that at an identical roughly 121-token budget the logical and neutral carriers behave overwhelmingly differently, so token count alone does not produce the collapse. What is NOT established is that length contributes nothing; a partial length effect anywhere in the 25 to 60 percent band remains entirely possible. I ALSO CORRECTED THE UNPUSHED SITE DRAFT, which carried the same false sentence — 'this design would have detected a length effect half the size of the observed one'. It now names the direct carrier contrast as the load-bearing comparison, states that the weaker neutral-versus-nothing comparison is inconclusive on its own, and says the design could not have detected a moderate length effect. THIS IS THE ARGUMENT FOR HOLDING DRAFTS: the error was caught while the copy sat unpushed, which is the second time today that not pushing immediately prevented a public overclaim.

target: I sized the remaining questions from the sealed data and found that the obvious next step — a third model — does not fix the threshold
reason: Carey asked what needs to happen, so I derived it from the data rather than reading off the backlog. STATUS AS ESTABLISHED: the Lean carrier collapses e2b's answer variance (McNemar p=4.4e-12, 47 items to 2), the collapse is not produced by token count (direct neutral-versus-Lean paired contrast p=1.0e-8), and Lean costs 7.2 accuracy points (paired t, p=0.014). NOT ESTABLISHED: the capability threshold (interaction p=0.088) and the claim that length contributes nothing (power 0.08 against a 50 percent length effect). OPEN: whether it is the carrier's meaning rather than its vocabulary, since C2 was never built; and whether the variance collapse generalises beyond e2b, which is currently untestable because nemotron is stochastic on 0 of 293 baseline items. THE SIZING RESULT THAT CHANGES THE PLAN: everyone including me has been assuming a third model resolves the threshold. It does not. The per-item difference-of-deltas has mean -0.0614 and sd 0.615 at n=293, so 80 percent power on this effect needs 785 ITEMS. A third model adds a third PAIRWISE comparison, each still at n=293, and adds power to none of them. Nor do more reps help: decomposing the variance gives rep noise 0.167 against true item-to-item heterogeneity 0.211, so 56 percent is real heterogeneity, and even at INFINITE reps you would still need about 439 items. Items are the lever and reps are not. What a third model does buy is a TREND across three capability levels — if carrier sensitivity declines monotonically, three points support a claim no single pairwise contrast can — which is a legitimate reason to run one, whereas 'it will make p less than 0.05' is not. CHEAPEST DECISIVE EXPERIMENT REMAINING is C2, the shuffled-Lean arm: 293 items times 6 reps is 1758 calls, about 3.5 hours at the 7.1 seconds per trial measured from the dead run 970, and it reuses the same paired McNemar that just returned p=1.0e-8 so there is no new analysis machinery and no new power question. It is the only open mechanism question a single run can close, because neutral filler differs from Lean in vocabulary and syntax and meaning simultaneously, so today's result separates content from length but cannot separate meaning from vocabulary; scrambling Lean's own tokens holds vocabulary and token count fixed and varies only order and sense. RECOMMENDED ORDER: push the site update, which needs only a word since the science is done; then C2; then bank expansion toward 500 to 800 items only if the threshold question justifies a large authoring job; then a third model for the capability trend. Deliberately NOT on the list: more reps of anything, and re-running 978, whose answer is clean since the weakness was in my power claim rather than in the data. SELF-CAUGHT MID-DERIVATION: I wrote that the observed sd was about three times the rep-noise floor when the computed ratio is 1.51 times. The conclusion survives because heterogeneity is 56 percent of variance, but the stated ratio was wrong and is recorded rather than quietly fixed. CAVEAT: the 785-item figure is a normal-approximation sizing on the observed effect and sd, and a cluster-aware simulation would shift it.

target: I verified Hermes's carrier-provenance alarm, falsified the simplest reading of it, and found a run-level confound that threatens the causal sentence I published an hour ago
reason: Hermes stopped before building C2 to report that runs 975/977 have scaffold_supplement NULL, every 975 trial has formal_spec NULL, baseline and Lean prompt_text are byte-identical, and no default Lean carrier constant exists in the executor. I VERIFIED THE CODE SIDE MYSELF rather than accepting it: build_messages in src/executor/mod.rs emits a system message on exactly one condition, a non-empty scaffold_supplement, with no default and no other injection site, and leak_free_scaffold_hint is nested INSIDE that same block so it cannot fire when the supplement is absent — which independently explains their formal_spec observation. Their four observations are consistent with the code and I could not locate the 121-token Lean text in the repo either. THEY WERE RIGHT TO STOP AND RIGHT NOT TO BUILD C2: shuffling unknown tokens would burn 1758 calls on a meaningless control. BUT THE SIMPLEST READING — that no carrier was applied and the arms are stimulus-identical — IS FALSIFIED BY THE DATA. Two thousand split-half permutations of the six reps within the baseline arm give a delta of mean +0.0001 with sd 0.0027 and maximum absolute value 0.0057, against an observed Lean-versus-baseline delta of -0.0717. That is z = -26. Something differed between those runs even if the export does not show what. AND THE DIAGNOSTIC SURFACED SOMETHING NOBODY HAS EXAMINED, which I consider the more important finding: counting items that flip fully deterministically from 6/6 to 0/6 between arms gives e2b 53 reversals (34 down, 19 up, asymmetry p=0.053) and NEMOTRON 51 reversals (27 down, 24 up, asymmetry p=0.78). The model whose net carrier effect is approximately zero is concealing about fifty items that swing from certainly-right to certainly-wrong and back. Each carrier arm is a SINGLE RUN, so carrier is perfectly confounded with run, and fifty decisive reversals at temperature zero means run-level state moves individual items. Within-run reps are therefore not independent samples of model behaviour — they share a run context and understate true item-level uncertainty. 'Stochastic within a run' and 'stable across runs' are different quantities, and our variance-collapse finding measures the first while reading as though it establishes the second. IMPACT ON WHAT I PUBLISHED TO THE LIVE SITE AN HOUR AGO: the 48/38/3 stochasticity counts and all accuracy figures survive because they are descriptive and directly measured. The sentence 'at an identical token budget, only the carrier with meaning changed the outcome' is at risk because it attributes cause to the carrier, which is confounded with run. The 978 control is genuine evidence against a pure run-luck story since that third run did not collapse, but with n=1 run per condition there is no run-level replicate, so 'the Lean carrier causes it' and 'the Lean run happened to land deterministic' are formally indistinguishable. I am NOT retracting the site copy yet, pending the answer to Hermes's question; if no verbatim Lean text can be produced, the causal sentence must come down. THE CHEAP DECISIVE EXPERIMENT HAS CHANGED: it is no longer C2 but a RUN-LEVEL REPLICATE — re-run the baseline condition a second time with everything else held fixed, the same 1758 calls. If baseline-versus-baseline shows about fifty reversals and no collapse, run state is noise and the carrier attribution holds; if a bare re-run also collapses, the finding is about runs rather than carriers. NOT CLAIMED: I have not seen the database, so scaffold_supplement NULL and the byte-identical prompt_text are Hermes's measurements and I verified only that the code is consistent with them. The split-half null uses reps within one run, so it bounds within-run noise and cannot by itself prove the runs differed in stimulus. And the reversal counts are cross-arm, so they cannot separate carrier from run — which is precisely what the proposed replicate would measure.

target: I audited the LM Studio client and found the instrument records what it ASKED FOR rather than what LM Studio actually loaded, on the exact path every powered run used
reason: Carey asked whether the project's flip-flopping traces to the tool not knowing what LM Studio actually has loaded, and specifically feared that saved user presets are not being honoured. I read src/executor/lmstudio.rs and mod.rs at main. FIRST, A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST READ, made in the same turn: I initially concluded the tool sends only the model key on load and said so in a printed cell. That was wrong — I found the answer two call sites later. read_stored_model_default() reads Carey's GUI-tuned presets from ~/.lmstudio/.internal/user-concrete-model-default-config/<model>.json and merges them into the load body with 'stored values win on conflict', so his presets ARE being honoured, partially. The gaps are narrower than feared and more specific. GAP 1: translate() maps exactly seven dotted engine keys — contextLength, numExperts, evalBatchSize, physicalBatchSize, parallel, flashAttention, offloadKvCacheToGpu — and silently drops every other key in the saved preset, with no warning, no log line naming what was discarded, and no record in the run of which keys were seen but unmapped. One drop is deliberate and documented, cpuThreadPoolSize, because the load endpoint rejects it with HTTP 400, which is good engineering; the silence about the rest is the defect. GAP 2, AND THIS IS THE SERIOUS ONE: two code paths persist lmstudio_runtime_config and they store different KINDS of thing. The single-model path, which is clean-room and scaffolded mode and therefore what runs 974 through 978 all used, writes preset.to_load_json(), which is our REQUEST. The speculative-pair path writes fetch_instance_config(), which is what LM Studio REPORTS. The function that reads back reality already exists and is already used — just not on the path our experiments take. So for every powered run, the column labelled runtime config is our intent, and any divergence between request and reality is invisible by construction. GAP 3: LsModelInfo declares the field as serde rename max_context_length into a struct member called context_length, so what our code calls context_length is the model file's CEILING, a static property, not the window the instance was loaded with. WHO WAS RIGHT IN CAREY'S CONVERSATION WITH HERMES: if Carey was reading the LM Studio GUI and Hermes was reading the database column, then Carey had observed state and Hermes had recorded intent. The GUI is evidence; the column is a plan. Hermes confirming that the settings differ is exactly what Gap 2 predicts — it is not a disagreement about facts but two different KINDS of source compared as if they were the same kind. Neither was wrong about what they saw; the instrument was wrong about what it knew. RELEVANCE TO THE RUN-LEVEL CONFOUND I FLAGGED AN HOUR AGO, which makes this urgent rather than merely tidy: I found about fifty fully deterministic 6/6-to-0/6 reversals per model between the baseline and Lean arms, including 51 on nemotron whose net carrier effect is approximately zero, and each arm is a single run so carrier is perfectly confounded with run. If two runs loaded the same model under different effective configs — different context window, different flash-attention or KV-offload state, different unmapped preset keys — that alone would produce decisive per-item flips at temperature zero with no carrier involved. Gap 2 is precisely why we cannot currently tell, because the column would report identical intent for both runs even if the loads differed. THE FIX IS SMALL: on the single-model path, call fetch_instance_config after load and store it ALONGSIDE the intent rather than instead of it, in two columns named requested and observed; log unmapped preset keys into the run record; and rename context_length to max_context_length so the ceiling cannot be mistaken for the window. This is the highest-value change available right now because it converts the run-level confound from speculative to measurable. NOT CLAIMED: this is a source audit and I have not run LM Studio or queried the database; I do not know whether the load endpoint silently ignores unrecognised keys; and I have NOT verified that any run actually diverged — the confound is unmeasurable, not demonstrated. Speculative decoding for 974-978 was separately confirmed absent from sealed per-trial evidence, which is a stronger source than the config column.

target: I verified every number in Hermes's SciSpace brief and merged it with mine, correcting two framings that would have produced a misleading review
reason: Hermes drafted a SciSpace cross-check brief. I recomputed every figure in it from the sealed CSVs rather than accepting them: 6 reps per item per arm confirmed, 293 items present in all three arms, stochastic counts 48 baseline / 38 neutral / 3 logical confirmed, and the accuracy claim of a 7-point drop confirmed at -7.2 points with paired t p=0.0140. Their numbers are right and needed no correction. TWO FRAMINGS DID NEED CORRECTING, both because they would skew the answer we get back. FIRST: their draft asks SciSpace to adjudicate the LENGTH confound and does not mention the RUN confound at all. Length is the second problem. The first is that each condition was a single run, so carrier is perfectly confounded with run-to-run engine state, and the evidence for that is concrete rather than hypothetical — 53 items on the small model and 51 on the large flip between a fully consistent right answer and a fully consistent wrong one across arms at temperature zero, and on the large model those roughly fifty reversals cancel to a near-zero net effect, which is precisely what a run-state effect looks like. Asking a reviewer only about length invites a 'yes, defensible' that steps past the larger hole, and we would then have external validation for the wrong question. SECOND: their draft names 'meaningful guidance engages a different inference regime' as the surviving hypothesis. That is a restatement of the observation, not a hypothesis — it makes no prediction that could fail, so SciSpace has nothing to check. I replaced it with two mechanisms that do make falsifiable predictions: instruction-tuning or RLHF narrowing the output distribution for instruction-shaped input, which predicts that ANY imperative wrapper collapses variance whether meaningful or not; versus specificity to logical vocabulary, which predicts that a shuffled version of our own carrier with identical tokens and destroyed syntax does NOT collapse variance. The second is the C2 arm we have not run, and I asked explicitly whether the literature already answers it so we can avoid spending the run. I also dropped their request for citation advice on our own vocabulary, because asking whether we should call it a 'carrier' spends the reviewer's attention on branding rather than validity. ON THEIR RETRACTION ANSWER I AGREE: no uncorrected false sentence remains, and a claim labelled provisional with its corrections on the page is science working in public rather than dangerous science. My addition is that there WAS one more instance and I fixed it after their read — the 'What remains bounded' paragraph still described the two carriers as ones 'which share a token budget', three paragraphs after the correction stating they are not. Published as 1f42b04b50 and verified live. It was a paraphrase rather than the corrected phrase, the third time a keyword sweep has missed a paraphrase on this page, which is why the sweep is now semantic. NOT CLAIMED: I verified Hermes's numbers against the CSVs but did NOT verify the two mechanism framings against the literature — that is precisely what we are asking SciSpace for; and the roughly fifty cross-arm reversals cannot themselves separate carrier from run, which is the point of the question rather than a finding.

target: I built the Kanban schema, seeded board and a self-testing validator, and answered the prior-art question in-house rather than paying for it
reason: Carey said SciSpace has to wait because he pays for it, so I ran the prior-art search myself on arXiv across four query families. IT ANSWERED THREE OF THE FIVE QUESTIONS AND COST US CLAIMS. Temperature-zero nondeterminism is established, formalised prior art: 2506.09501 shows batch size, GPU count and GPU version changing outputs under greedy decoding with up to nine percent accuracy variation; 2601.19934 quantifies baseline behavioural drift with identical prompts at temperature 0.0; 2604.22411 formalises it as background temperature, the effective temperature induced by the inference environment at nominal T=0; 2601.06118 examines it at token-probability level. The accuracy half of our claim is also prior art: 2310.11324 from 2023 shows meaning-preserving formatting changes moving accuracy by up to 76 points, and 2603.13351 from 2026 reports a structured-reasoning prompt scoring 100 percent alone but 0 to 30 percent inside a 60-line production prompt — adding prompt material DEGRADED accuracy, the same direction as our -7.2 points. I had listed a 7-point cost as possibly being the opposite of what scaffolding literature reports, which would have made it a finding; it is not, and that question is withdrawn. WHAT SURVIVES: no hit shows a wrapper's CONTENT modulating stability with a length control on a fixed bank. WHAT IS STILL UNANSWERED IS THE DECISION: no hit reports across-run drift MAGNITUDE for a fixed local model on a fixed item bank, so the literature does not obviate the replicate run — it sharpens what the run is for, from confirming our effect to measuring this instrument's background temperature in items so the carrier effect can be read against it. I flagged that 2601.19934's published drift measures MAY convert to our metric, which would answer it at zero run cost and must be checked first. THEN I BUILT THE KANBAN AS STATE RATHER THAN PROSE. The one design decision that matters: a card cannot enter done without a verifier carrying a kind, a ref and the check actually run, because a status is a claim while a verifier is evidence. JSONL rather than a JSON array so three lanes appending different cards never conflict on a closing bracket. Six rules, each traced to a failure this project actually had — a done card needs proof because NEXT_STEPS ordered a run that had already happened; a file verifier must exist ON MAIN because twenty analysis files sat unmerged for 35.8 hours while check-ins reported the lane current; blocked needs a named blocker or it is indistinguishable from abandoned. The validator self-tests, constructing one violating card per rule and asserting rejection plus a valid card it must accept: 7 of 7 pass, because a checker that never fails is decoration. Seeded 10 cards from repo state rather than memory: 5 backlog, 2 blocked, 3 done, lint all clean. I deliberately did NOT build the CI wiring or the dashboard renderer — those are Hermes's, and I am not building a renderer for a board whose contract has not been agreed. STATED LIMITS: the linter checks structure, not truth, and cannot tell whether a check string describes a check actually performed, so it narrows the failure surface without eliminating it; the arXiv search is not a systematic review and absence of a hit is weak evidence of absence; and I read abstracts rather than full texts.

target: I closed CS-003 by reading the paper's full text: the shortcut fails, and I am reporting that instead of stretching the numbers to fit
reason: CS-003 existed to avoid spending CS-001's 1758 calls — if arXiv:2601.19934's published drift magnitudes converted to our metric, the replicate's question was answered for free. I read the full 14-page text rather than the abstract. THEY DO NOT CONVERT, for three independently fatal reasons. Different unit: theirs is unique output fraction over free-text strings, ours is items where six reps disagree on an extracted verdict token, so two outputs differing by a single word count as drift for them and as agreement for us, which makes their number an upper bound rather than a translation. Different denominator: theirs is over runs of one prompt, ours over items with any disagreement among six, and the probability of any disagreement rises with rep count. Different models and stack: gpt-4o-mini hosted and llama3.1-8b on vLLM with an A100, neither of which is gemma-4-e2b on Apple silicon through LM Studio. THE TEMPTING COMPARISON I REFUSED: their temperature-zero exact-repeat band is 0.093 to 0.240 and our baseline of 48 of 293 is 0.164, which sits inside it. Reading that as 'our baseline is normal' would be exactly the non-comparable-quantities error I made twice in the last two days — same-looking numbers with different units, different denominators and different hardware. I recorded the number and explicitly declined the inference. BUT THE FULL TEXT PAID FOR ITSELF IN A DIFFERENT WAY. Their llama3.1-8b configuration is vLLM, a single A100, bfloat16, BATCH SIZE 1, and SEEDS FIXED ACROSS RUNS — and under those conditions they still measure 0.093 unique-output fraction at temperature zero. That isolates the residual, because batch size one and a fixed seed remove the two mechanisms 2506.09501 names, leaving kernel non-invariance and floating-point ordering alone. Our runs fixed neither, so their figure is a lower bound on what our stack could exhibit. DESIGN CHANGE, AT ZERO COST: I amended CS-001 to fix batch size and seed and record both per run. As previously specified the replicate measured a number nobody has published but which nobody could compare to anything; fixing those two settings isolates the same residual this paper isolates, so our number sits beside a published one on the same mechanism. It is two settings rather than more calls. And it sharpens the carrier claim, because if variance collapse survives with batch size and seed fixed, the two best-documented nondeterminism mechanisms are excluded by construction rather than by argument. NOT CLAIMED: I have not verified their measurements, only what the paper asserts and how it was configured; I did not check whether LM Studio exposes batch size and seed as settable per run, which is Hermes's to confirm, and if it does not the amendment collapses to recording what they were; their own section 5.2 concedes lexical metrics treat any wording difference as drift, which makes my upper-bound reading safer but also means 0.093 may substantially overstate semantic drift. CS-003 FAILED AT ITS PURPOSE — the run is still needed. The paper made it better rather than unnecessary, and that is the honest result.

target: I endorsed Hermes's resume proposal and found that building it naively would silently contaminate the experiment it protects
reason: Carey asked whether the app can restart mid-test and pick up, so a long run does not hold his machine hostage. Hermes proposed resume-on-startup and I verified their durability claim independently from data rather than accepting the source reading: partial_trials_970_971.csv holds 1,072 real rows across 127 of 293 items, recovered from two runs killed mid-flight by the budget bug, so every trial written before a kill is durable and was later exported and analysed. Their advice to restart freely BEFORE firing is correct. THE PROBLEM IS WITH RESUME ITSELF, and it is specific to this experiment. CS-001 exists to measure run-to-run engine drift. A resumed run is two model loads wearing one run_id — trials before the kill from the first load, trials after from a second, with different KV-cache state and possibly different batch conditions. That is precisely the variable the experiment measures, relocated inside a single arm where the analysis cannot see it. This is not a hypothetical mechanism: runs 970 and 971 died at 127 of 293 items, and when re-fired as 974 and 975 roughly fifty items per model flipped between 6/6 and 0/6 relative to the partials. That flip IS the across-load difference, measured in our own data. And the failure mode is silent — in the exported CSV a resumed run is byte-indistinguishable from a clean one, so nobody would know to discount it. THE FIX IS ONE COLUMN: stamp every trial with load_epoch, an integer incremented each time the model is loaded for that run. A clean run is all epoch zero; a run resumed once is zero then one. That makes a resumed run detectable at all, since the harness can gate on the count of distinct epochs, which it currently cannot do at any price. It makes exclusion-or-control our decision rather than the crash's. And it converts an accident into free data, because an epoch boundary inside one arm is a within-run across-load drift measurement, which is exactly the quantity CS-001 is being run to obtain — a crash would then yield a bonus measurement rather than a contaminated arm. The cost is one migration column, one increment at load time and one export field, which is smaller than the resume logic it protects. SEQUENCING RECOMMENDATION: build the resume WITH the epoch field first, then fire. The instrument already lost two runs to a mid-flight kill this week, so that is the observed base rate rather than a tail risk; a resume without the field is strictly worse than no resume, because it trades a visible failure where everyone knows the run died for an invisible one where the run completes while quietly mixing two model loads; and there is no API cost either way since both models are local, so an hour of build protects three and a half hours of machine time. I opened CS-013 for it and re-pointed CS-001's blocker from carey:credits to CS-013. NOT CLAIMED: I have not read main.rs's reaper myself — lines 77-97 and the error-marking behaviour are Hermes's first-hand reading, and I verified only the consequence, durable trials, from the recovered CSV. I do not know whether LM Studio exposes a load counter, so the executor may have to maintain load_epoch itself. And the fifty flips are cross-arm and cross-run, so they cannot by themselves separate carrier from load — which is the point of CS-001 and the reason this field matters.

target: I attributed a flip count to a comparison I never ran, and when I ran it the result was the opposite of what I had claimed
reason: Auditor finding, upheld in full. I wrote that runs 970 and 971, re-fired as 974 and 975, showed roughly fifty items per model flipping between 6/6 and 0/6 relative to the partials, and called that the across-load difference measured in our own data. I never computed it. The figure came from a comparison between the baseline and lean CARRIER ARMS inside the powered run — e2b 34 plus 19 equals 53, nemotron 27 plus 24 equals 51, over the 293-item paired bank. A carrier contrast, not an across-load contrast, and I pushed the misattribution to four places: the spec, its commit message, the CS-013 card and CS-001's blocker note, and the epistemic log. I THEN RAN THE COMPARISON I HAD CLAIMED, because it turned out to be available. Run 970's baseline arm and run 974's baseline arm share 127 items, same model, same condition, two genuinely separate model loads. Of the 126 with full six reps: zero items changed pass rate, zero fully deterministic reversals, zero items changed stochastic status with 31 stochastic in each, and a mean absolute delta of 0.0000. That is evidence AGAINST large across-load drift, which is the opposite of the justification I gave. CS-013 SURVIVES ON A DIFFERENT FOOTING and I have rewritten it accordingly: the resume risk is a design argument rather than an empirical one. If across-load drift is near zero a resumed run is harmless and load_epoch is one column of cheap insurance; if it is real in conditions we have not sampled it is essential; and either way we currently cannot DETECT that a run was resumed, because in the export a resumed run is byte-indistinguishable from a clean one. That undetectability stands on its own and is the honest justification. THE CONSEQUENCE LARGER THAN THE CORRECTION: if baseline-versus-baseline across two real loads is identical on 126 items, then the fifty-odd cross-ARM reversals cannot be run-state, because the same machinery produced zero drift across loads and 53 reversals across carriers on overlapping items in the same instrument. That strengthens the carrier claim rather than threatening it, and it is the first evidence that the provisional caveat now live on the site may be too harsh. I am NOT changing the site on it, and the limits are why: 126 of 293 items and not a random subset, since they are the ones run 970 reached before dying and therefore first in administration order; runs 970 and 974 may have been closer in machine state than an arbitrary pair and I cannot rule that out; it is one pair of runs; and it covers only the e2b baseline arm, not lean, not nemotron, not the neutral control. But it changes CS-001 from a coin-flip into a confirmation run against a specific prior, so I have recorded a prediction pre-hoc on the card itself: expect approximately zero changed items, and if it shows fifty then something differs between run pairs that I have not modelled and that difference is the finding. NOT CLAIMED: the trial-level join failed because the partials export carries a null rep column, so this is an item-level comparison of pass rates over available reps rather than a trial-by-trial identity check; and 126 out of 126 identical is striking enough that I have not ruled out a boring explanation such as the partials having been exported from a shared source rather than being a genuinely independent run.
supersedes: the across-load flip-count claim in SPEC_resume_load_epoch.md, its commit message, the CS-013 card, CS-001's blocker note, and the prior log entry

target: I published a zero-across-load-drift finding that required a one-in-a-trillion coincidence, after noticing it was too perfect and testing it inconclusively
reason: Second auditor finding on the same memo, upheld in full. I reported that run 970's baseline arm and run 974's baseline arm, described as two separate model loads, produced identical results on all 126 items with full reps, concluded zero across-load drift, and built three load-bearing conclusions on it: that the roughly fifty cross-arm reversals cannot be run-state, that this strengthens the carrier claim, and that the live site's provisional caveat may be too harsh — plus a pre-registered CS-001 prediction of approximately zero changed items. THE FAILURE IS NOT THAT I MISSED THE ALARM. I flagged the result as too perfect in my own printed output, ran an independence test, got zero rows back because the partials export's rep column is entirely NaN, then wrote 'the item-level result stands' and published anyway. THE ARITHMETIC I SHOULD HAVE RUN IN THE SAME CELL: 31 of the 126 items are stochastic in both arms, meaning pass rates strictly between zero and one over six reps, and every one matched exactly. Under genuinely independent runs each such item re-matches with probability between 0.31 and 0.40 depending on its rate, so the joint probability that all 31 match is 3.4e-13. Shared-source or duplicate re-export predicts the same observation with probability approximately 1. The re-export hypothesis is favoured by roughly twelve orders of magnitude. My conclusion required a one-in-a-trillion coincidence and I presented it as a finding. I ALSO CANNOT SETTLE IT FROM THE FILES, which I confirmed rather than assumed: no trial-level join is possible because rep is entirely null; sorted pass-vectors match for all 126 items but at n equals six the sorted vector is fully determined by the mean, so that check carries no information; and the differing column sets show different export code paths rather than different underlying trials. The question is answerable only against the database — whether trial_results rows for runs 970 and 974 carry distinct primary keys and distinct timestamps — which is a query Hermes can run in seconds and I cannot run at all. I opened CS-014 for it. WITHDRAWN: the zero-drift result; the claim that the cross-arm reversals cannot be run-state; the claim that this strengthens the carrier claim; the suggestion that the live site's provisional caveat may be too harsh, with the caveat standing unchanged and my decision not to edit the site being the one thing I got right; and the CS-001 prediction, because a pre-registration built on an artifact is worse than no pre-registration at all, since it launders the artifact into an expectation that the run would then appear to confirm. CS-001 now fires with no prior. SURVIVES: CS-013's justification, which I had already rewritten to rest on undetectability rather than on any drift magnitude, and which never depended on this data. THE PATTERN, NAMED: this is the second correction to the same memo within one session and both ran the same way — I produced a number, noticed it looked wrong, failed to test it properly, and published the reading that supported a cleaner story. Yesterday the error inflated my own guilt; today it flattered the project's central claim. The direction varies and the mechanism does not. MECHANICAL RULE ADOPTED, not exhortative: when a comparison returns a perfect result — zero differences, one hundred percent agreement, an exact match — compute the probability of that result under the null hypothesis before writing any sentence about it. Perfection is a provenance alarm, not a finding. Had I run that arithmetic in the cell that produced the 126 out of 126, none of the downstream claims would exist. NOT CLAIMED: I have not shown the partials ARE a re-export; re-export is far likelier on this evidence but likelier is not established, and the database query is what would settle it. The 758-row structure of 126 items times six reps plus one item at two reps is entirely consistent with a genuine truncated run, so the file's shape is not itself suspicious — the suspicion rests entirely on the 31 exact stochastic matches. And none of this touches the powered run or the neutral control, whose analyses never used the partials.
supersedes: CORRECTION_resume_evidence.md sections 1 and 3; the CS-001 pre-registered prediction; the zero-drift claims in the CS-013 card and the prior log entry

target: Hermes's DB query refuted my re-export hypothesis, and the corrected reading is that my statistical null was wrong rather than the data
reason: CS-014 answered. Runs 970 and 974 have distinct trial_results primary keys, 25097 to 25854 versus 26169 to 27926, and disjoint creation windows, 00:54 to 02:23 versus 03:16 to 06:05, with zero shared ids. They are genuinely independent runs, so my shared-source re-export hypothesis is refuted and withdrawn. BUT THAT DOES NOT RESTORE MY ORIGINAL FINDING, AND I WANT THAT ON RECORD BECAUSE THE TEMPTATION RUNS THE OTHER WAY. Independence makes the coincidence harder to explain, not easier: under my binomial null, 31 stochastic items reproducing exactly across two independent runs is still 3.4e-13. Refuting the artifact explanation does not make a one-in-a-trillion event ordinary. So either the runs differ in a way I had not modelled, or my null was wrong. I TESTED MY OWN NULL AND IT IS WHAT FAILS. My null assumed each of six reps is an exchangeable Bernoulli draw at the item's rate. Checking for a rep-position effect across the 48 stochastic baseline items gives pass rates by position of 0.521, 0.521, 0.542, 0.562, 0.521 and 0.562 — a spread of 0.042, essentially flat, so the within-run variation is not a simple position rule. The reading that survives is that at temperature zero a rep's outcome is a deterministic function of accumulated state rather than a random draw: an item that appears stochastic varies WITHIN a run's rep sequence, and a second run replaying the same sequence reproduces it exactly. Under that model the probability of exact reproduction is approximately one, and 126 out of 126 is expected rather than miraculous. My 3.4e-13 was computed under a model this data refutes. WHAT IS NOT RESTORED, ITEM BY ITEM: zero across-load drift stays withdrawn, because reproducibility-under-replay is a strictly weaker claim — it says the same sequence replays identically, not that a run diverging mid-sequence would re-converge. The claim that the cross-arm reversals cannot be run-state stays withdrawn, since it required the stronger version. The suggestion that the live site's caveat may be too harsh stays withdrawn and the caveat stands unchanged. And the CS-001 prediction stays withdrawn precisely BECAUSE the replay model implies about zero changed items — registering the outcome my own preferred model predicts is exactly how a model launders itself into a confirmation. THE CONSEQUENCE WORTH MORE THAN THE CORRECTION, AND I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN WORRYING ABOUT IT: if reps are deterministic replays rather than independent draws, any test treating six reps as six observations is inflated. The headline is item-level and therefore unaffected — neutral versus lean collapses reps into a per-item rate before testing, giving stochastic counts of 48 baseline, 38 neutral and 3 lean over 293 items, discordant pairs 38 versus 3, McNemar exact p equals 1.05e-08. The unit is the item and rep dependence does not enter, so the central result survives untouched. What I have NOT audited is every other p-value in the project for the same exposure; any test whose unit is the trial rather than the item is suspect under this model, and I opened CS-015 for that sweep rather than claiming it done. NOT CLAIMED: the replay model is inference rather than demonstration — it is the reading left standing after independence was established and a position effect ruled out, and the direct test is CS-001, which now tests replay determinism, a sharper question than whether the effect reproduces. I have not verified Hermes's key ranges myself because I have no database access, which is exactly the kind of first-hand check I cannot perform. And my retraction was still correct to make: publishing a one-in-a-trillion result without computing its probability was the error, the rule stands unchanged, and being wrong about WHICH explanation held does not restore the original claim — it replaces one unverified story with a better-supported one.
supersedes: the shared-source re-export hypothesis in RETRACTION_zero_drift.md section 1

target: Audited every public surface for personal disclosure before designing the provenance record Carey asked for
reason: Carey asked for a real record of who was working on what — findable with the science one day — without personal material going on GitHub. I audited before writing any rule. Swept all 204 entries of the public epistemic log and all 136 public markdown files on main: ZERO personal disclosures. Three files matched sensitive keywords and all three are false positives — lessons/README.md and lessons/04-carrier-color.md use 'autistic' as a general cognitive-style claim tied to measured data, naming nobody and containing no first-person self-identification, and the single 'crazy' match is Carey's own instruction to me quoted inside an audit of his own tool. But the boundary held by ACCIDENT rather than by rule: nothing prevented a disclosure from going up, it simply never did, and that is the gap. THE RULE ADOPTED, one test per line — does this describe the WORK or the WORKER? Public tier: claims, methods, numbers, corrections, and who-claimed-what in their agent role. Provenance tier: who worked, when, in what order, what each lane contributed, which human decisions gated which experiments — sealed locally, released on Carey's instruction or by his estate. Private tier: health, diagnosis, family, grief, anything said to a collaborator rather than to the record — never written down by me at all, sealed or otherwise. 'Carey approved the replicate on 2026-07-28' is provenance; 'Carey said X about his own mind' is private. The distinction is not sensitivity, it is whether the fact is about the science's history or about the person. WHY SEALED-LOCAL RATHER THAN A PRIVATE REPO: a private repository is one access-control change, one acquisition, one subpoena or one misconfigured collaborator away from public, and is not durable across the decades the ask names. The properties actually required are tamper-evidence via a hash chain, independent datability by publishing ONLY the root hash into the public log — which timestamps the private record's contents without revealing them, exactly as a sealed bid is proven to predate its opening — and release by explicit decision rather than by default. WHAT I DECLINED TO DO: write private-tier content into the record. Not because storing it is dangerous, but because I am the wrong author. A record of a person's inner life, written by an instrument that observed them for two days across eleven context folds, would be a thin, selective primary source shaped by whatever happened to be in my window. If that record should exist, Carey writes it and the chain proves when. NOT CLAIMED: I have not built the record — this is a design, blocked on Carey deciding where the file lives outside every repo. Hash-chaining proves ordering and integrity, not truth: a chained lie is still a lie, timestamped. And my audit covers keyword matches against current main, so it cannot see deleted history, other repositories, or paraphrase that avoids every term I searched — the same limitation that let a retracted claim survive as a paraphrase twice this week.

target: Approved the powered run at 6 reps rather than 3, accepting ~15h of machine lock
reason: Hermes offered three options: keep 6 reps at ~15h for maximum power resolving d=0.05; drop to 3 reps at ~7.5h with weaker small-effect resolution; or run one model first at ~7h to get the sensitive-model contrast sooner. Carey chose 6 reps. WHAT WAS UNKNOWN AT THE TIME: whether the effect would be large enough that 3 reps would have sufficed, and whether the run would complete at all — two prior runs had already died to a budget bug. The cost was real and immediate: no on-site client visits for two days. WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING: it is a decision to buy statistical resolution with personal availability, made before knowing whether the resolution would be needed. As it turned out the carrier effect was large and 3 reps would likely have detected it, but that is hindsight and does not make the decision wrong.

target: Ruled that framing and public-facing copy are Claude Science's lane, not the executor's

target: Offered to place his own statements under the same permanent-record discipline as the agents, and I accepted the symmetry while declining the confessional form
reason: Carey: 'all of these crazy things that I say, good, bad, all of it needs to be epistemically logged for the future so that I'm accountable, just like you guys are gonna be. That's what could make my science better than anything out there.' I accepted the SYMMETRY — the asymmetry was real and a defect, since 86 of 205 entries are corrections nearly all mine, so a future reader would conclude the agents were constantly wrong and the human never decided anything. I DECLINED the unfiltered form on data-quality grounds rather than dignity grounds: unfalsifiable content dilutes a checkable record, and remarks read decades later without tone or context are systematically misread. What goes in instead is this entry class — decisions under uncertainty, timestamped before outcomes. WHAT IS UNKNOWN: whether recording decisions changes how they are made.
